519183|2026-03.headline: ADF Foods Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue hit a record INR196.7 crore (+23.7% YoY), with EBITDA margin at 17.4%, but Middle East (GCC) exposure clouds FY27 guidance.
519183|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue rose 23.7% YoY to a record INR196.7 crore, with EBITDA of INR34.3 crore (17.4% margin, +190 bps) and PAT of INR25.9 crore (+57.6%). Standalone FY26 revenue grew 10.3% to INR527.9 crore with EBITDA margin of 24.8%. The Surat greenfield plant began commercial production in March 2026, but West Asia disruption stopped GCC shipments in March and April, and management cut its outlook to a conditional range if the disruption persists. Net cash surplus stands at INR78.2 crore and the final dividend is 30% of face value (60% for FY26).

segments.name: Ashoka (flagship brand)
segments.commentary: Management guided Ashoka to grow about 30-35% in FY27; FY26 Ashoka revenue was about INR308 crore per an analyst's calculation that management did not dispute. Core markets are North America (incl. Canada), UK and Europe, with Australia and New Zealand also growing.

segments.name: Truly Indian (mainstream US brand)
segments.commentary: Management expects Truly Indian revenue of INR75-80 crore in FY27 if things go well. Listed in about 3,000 US stores including Costco, Raley's, Safeway-Albertsons and Whole Foods; repeat rotations are seen at some Costco divisions.

segments.name: B2B and private label
segments.commentary: B2B and private label make up about 20% of revenue. Distribution business added new regional brands and Ashoka SKUs (staples, oils, flour), with SKUs rising from about 440 to about 600.

segments.name: GCC / Middle East
segments.commentary: About 15% of revenue (described as under 15%). Shipments were nil in March and about 80-85% of GCC business was lost, with only 1-2 ports operating in April.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of INR925-1,000 crore, conditional on West Asia stabilising within about a month; management said it would revisit guidance if disruption continues.
If GCC contribution stays at zero, FY27 growth is about 12-15% (roughly INR800-850 crore); with GCC normalised, growth of 30%+ and the INR925-1,000 crore band.
Surat plant expected to contribute INR40-50 crore revenue in FY27; full capacity implies upwards of INR200-250 crore (Phase 2 included), with full utilisation targeted in year 3.
Management expects to maintain high-teen consolidated EBITDA margins; Surat margins at full capacity expected to be similar to existing facilities.
Freight costs up about 3-4% of revenue in March; management said this is expected to ease over about the next two months. Analyst was told to add about 1 percentage point of freight in the base.
PLI incentive expected to be similar in FY27 (about INR16 crore) and is the final year of the scheme.
Capex of INR20-25 crore in FY27 (pizza base line, Surat balance payments), plus INR15-20 crore for Nadiad and Nashik debottlenecking; a further US warehouse is planned around Q3 FY27.
Potential INR30 crore quarterly revenue risk from GCC on a run-rate basis, as an analyst framed it and management confirmed.
capex_capacity: Approximately INR124 crore capex over the last 2 years across Nadiad, Nashik brownfield and Surat greenfield; Surat total investment including Phase 2 is a little above INR100 crore.
Surat Phase 1 (2 product lines) commenced production in the third week of March 2026; Phase 2 adds a product line (pizza base) in Q3 FY27.
Surat utilisation expected at about 35-40% in Phase 1 during FY27; Phase 2 contributes only 10-15% utilisation in FY27.
Average capacity utilisation across product lines was about 70-75% in FY26.
US warehouse: freezer space above 100% utilised (using outside storage); ambient space about 85% utilised. Another distribution centre planned, probably in Q3 FY27.
Debottlenecking at Nadiad and Nashik (flatbread and snack lines) drove most of the FY26 volume growth.
demand_pricing: Q4 FY26 growth was about 60-65% volume-driven, with the balance from product mix and rupee depreciation; management said prices were not increased.
Truly Indian initial traction is mainly distribution-led, with some repeats at Costco and other chains; management sees the Indian ethnic category at an inflection point in the US mainstream channel.
No impact seen from GLP-1 drugs (Ozempic) on demand; the whole range is vegetarian and vegan.
GCC shipments were nil in March 2026 because shipping lines were not taking containers. Other markets saw longer transit times and higher freight rates but no loss of sales.
Freight costs rose sharply in March 2026 as vessels were jammed and US routes lengthened; the company shares freight cost with GCC distributors 50:50 on those routes.
Tariff refund: applications filed for upwards of USD 1.5 million following a Supreme Court directive; nothing received in FY26, and any refund will be accrued in the year received.

qa_highlights.question: How does FY27 guidance of INR925-1,000 crore reconcile with the growth drivers, given Ashoka and Truly Indian?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the INR925-1,000 crore band, conditional on the Middle East reopening. Ashoka is expected to grow 30-35% and Truly Indian INR75-80 crore. With zero GCC, growth is 12-15% (about INR800-850 crore).

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East (GCC) impact and worst-case scenario?
qa_highlights.answer: GCC is under 15% of revenue. About 80-85% of GCC business has been lost, with nil March shipments. In the zero-GCC case, FY27 growth is about 12-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Surat plant ramp-up and revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 Surat contribution is INR40-50 crore; full capacity implies INR200-250 crore once Phase 2 is complete. Full utilisation is targeted in year 3.

qa_highlights.question: How much freight-cost increase should be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight rose by about 3-4% of revenue in March. The CFO said about 1 percentage point should be added to the base, with normalisation expected over about two months.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plans and total Surat spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Surat total is a little above INR100 crore. FY27 capex is INR20-25 crore (pizza line and balance payments) plus INR15-20 crore for Nadiad and Nashik debottlenecking.

qa_highlights.question: Will PLI incentive continue after FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 is the final year of the PLI scheme, expected at a similar level (about INR16 crore). The scheme covered 50% of marketing spend.

risks_watch: West Asia / GCC disruption: about 15% of revenue, with nil March shipments and only 1-2 ports open in April; guidance depends on normalisation within about 1-2 months.
Freight and logistics costs: March spike of about 3-4% of revenue; management expects normalisation but this is unproven.
Loss of PLI incentive after FY27 (about INR16 crore per year) will remove a support to margins.
Surat ramp-up: Phase 2 starts in Q3 FY27 and contributes only 10-15% utilisation in FY27; execution risk.
Freezer capacity in the US warehouse is above 100%, which requires outside storage and a new distribution centre.
519183|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the Q4 and FY26 results and on brand momentum, but cautious and conditional on guidance. Management repeatedly tied FY27 targets to a West Asia recovery and said it would revisit guidance if disruption continues; some answers on Middle East figures and the revenue bridge were vague.
key_quotes: So the Middle East has been -- I mean, because of the current situation in the month of March and April, we've not been able to service that market apart from a few ports because there are no shipping companies which are taking containers there.
So if the situation in the Middle East continues, of course, it will have an impact, and then we will look at revising our guidance.
The majority of the growth has come through with volume growth.
Surat total investment in Surat with Phase 2 completion will be a little above INR100 crores.

rows.why: Management expects to maintain high-teen consolidated EBITDA margins (FY26 at 19.1%, Q4 at 17.4%), but PLI support of about INR16 crore is the final year and freight is about 1 percentage point higher in the base, so expansion is not the message.

rows.why: Q4 FY26 growth was about 60-65% volume-driven, Ashoka guided to 30-35% growth in FY27, and average utilisation is 70-75%, but about 80-85% of the GCC business (about 15% of revenue) is lost for now.

rows.why: Utilisation averages 72.5% with freezer space above 100% at the US warehouse, so a further US distribution centre is planned for around Q3 FY27 alongside INR20-25 crore capex in FY27 plus INR15-20 crore debottlenecking.

rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance of INR925-1,000 crore is conditional on West Asia stabilising, and with zero GCC the growth is only 12-15% (about INR800-850 crore), so no upgrade is likely until the Middle East reopens.

rows.why: Management said it would revisit guidance if disruption continues; GCC shipments were nil in March and only 1-2 ports were open in April, with about 15% of revenue exposed and an analyst-framed risk of about INR30 crore quarterly revenue.

rows.label: Truly Indian US mainstream expansion
rows.why: Management expects Truly Indian revenue of INR75-80 crore in FY27 if things go well, from about 3,000 US stores including Costco, with repeat rotations at some Costco divisions.

rows.label: Tariff refund claim
rows.why: Applications filed for upwards of USD 1.5 million after a Supreme Court directive, with nothing received in FY26 and any refund to be accrued in the year received.

rows.label: PLI scheme ends after FY27
rows.why: FY27 is the final year of the PLI scheme at about INR16 crore, which the company's margins have relied on, so support falls away after FY27.

tone.note: Management was confident on Q4, FY26 results, brand momentum and the Surat ramp-up, but cautious and conditional on FY27 guidance tied to West Asia recovery; analysts pushed on the GCC impact, the revenue bridge and freight.

519183|2026-06.headline: ADF Foods Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 25.9% YoY to INR167.3 crore, but EBITDA margin of 17.7% was flattered by INR19.69 crore tariff refund; freight cost ~3% of revenue.
519183|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 25.9% YoY to INR167.3 crore, the fourth straight quarter of double-digit growth, with consolidated EBITDA up 26% to INR29.7 crore (17.7% margin) and PAT up 13.4% to INR17.3 crore. Management said the figures include tariff-refund benefit, and that adjusting for freight (~3% of revenue) the margin would be about 13.4% to 16.4% depending on the basis quoted on the call. Standalone revenue rose 20.5% to INR120.9 crore with EBITDA margin of 22.8%. Shipments were constrained by container and vessel shortages, with about 30% of ready goods unshipped in June, and management reiterated FY27 revenue above INR900 crore with high-teens EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Processed foods
segments.commentary: Revenue INR144 crore, up 28.5% YoY, with segment EBITDA of INR31.2 crore (21.6%). Management attributed the margin to product mix and frozen foods momentum.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: Revenue INR23.2 crore at 11.5% margin. Management said quarterly segment margins are seasonal and full-year margins will track historical ranges.

segments.name: Brands (Ashoka, Truly Indian, Soul)
segments.commentary: Ashoka growing above 30% in the latest quarter, with a 5-year revenue CAGR above 20%. Truly Indian is in 3,000+ US stores, with about 60% of growth from existing stores and 40% from new listings. Soul relaunch is still slow.

segments.name: B2B / private label
segments.commentary: Management put the sales split at about 75% own brands and 25% B2B and private label.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue upwards of INR900 crore, conditional on geopolitical and shipping conditions easing.
High-teens EBITDA margin guided for FY27 and beyond, excluding tariff refunds; management expects a return to 16-17% over about nine months as freight pass-through takes effect.
Freight pass-through began in Q1 FY27: about 75% in the US and 65-70% of total business overall, with some markets deliberately not passed on.
Surat revenue of about INR40-50 crore expected in FY27, with management saying the number is intact.
Surat full-scale utilisation expected in 2-3 years; about 30% utilisation this year and full utilisation around FY30.
Depreciation to rise by INR25-30 crore as Surat Phase 2 lines come in around Q3, with a further INR20-25 crore capex in FY27.
PLI scheme (about INR16 crore in FY26, about 2% of revenue) is in its final year; management hopes for an extension.
Q2 shipments expected to carry forward from Q1, but the carry-forward could slip into Q3 if container constraints persist.
Management said there are no further US tariff refunds expected; a USD2.8 million court award is under recovery discussion.
capex_capacity: Surat greenfield facility (frozen foods) began commercial deliveries and initial container shipments after commencing trial production in late March 2026; about 15 containers shipped in early Q1.
Surat at full capacity is expected to deliver a little under INR300 crore in revenue. Combined with brownfield capacity, total potential is about INR1,250 crore ex-agency at full ramp.
Phase 2 lines at Surat are expected in Q3, with residual capex of INR20-25 crore for FY27.
Management expects full utilisation of the combined capacity around FY30.
demand_pricing: Order book described as the strongest in company history for June, July and August, but about 30% of ready goods could not be shipped in June because of container and vessel shortages.
Management said consumer demand for ready-to-eat, frozen and shelf-stable Indian foods remains healthy across markets.
Pricing: freight costs passed through to customers from Q1 FY27 (about 3% of revenue impact). Tariff benefits will be passed back selectively by category to support market share.
Competition in Truly Indian is mainly from local US manufacturers of Indian-style foods, not Indian brands.
Management said the UK and Europe region should grow at high double digits, supported by a planned Ireland step-down subsidiary and FTAs.
West Asia disruption: March was very weak with no shipments; shipments resumed from end-April and are back near the 15% share of business previously affected.

qa_highlights.question: What is Surat's utilisation and when will it reach the INR275 crore target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said full capacity will take 2-3 years; about 30% utilisation expected this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the freight impact on margin and what is sustainable margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight impact about 3% of consolidated revenue; margin ex-freight was about 16.4% and about 13.4% after adjusting for tariff refund. Guidance is high-teens, with freight pass-through supporting recovery.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR900 crore revenue target achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it remains cautiously optimistic, conditional on easing geopolitical and shipping conditions; the order book and demand support it.

qa_highlights.question: Treatment of the remaining tariff refund balance in the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: The balance will be evaluated against customer arrangements and recognised over the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PLI contribution and its impact after FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: PLI was about INR16 crore in FY26 (about 2% of margin). Final year is FY27; management expects brand investment as a % of sales to fall as brands scale.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 see catch-up from Q1 shipment shortfall?
qa_highlights.answer: Some carry-forward is expected in Q2, but it could slip into Q3 if container availability does not improve.

risks_watch: Container and vessel availability; a carry-forward of unshipped goods could push revenue from Q2 into Q3.
Freight costs and whether pass-through holds in the US, where roughly 75% of freight increase is being passed on.
Tariff: the 10% rate is still applicable, with no certainty on the future rate.
Margin dependence on the one-time tariff refund and on PLI, which ends after FY27.
Surat ramp-up is slow (about 30% utilisation this year), which limits near-term operating leverage.
Soul domestic brand is growing slowly, while brand investments in Truly Indian and Soul continue.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR24 crore a year earlier per analyst

financial_highlights.value: USD2.08 million = INR19.69 crore received; USD0.77 million (~INR7 crore) booked in P&L in Q1

key_quotes: With strong business momentum, we remain well positioned to deliver revenue upwards of INR900 crores in financial year 27 while maintaining healthy high-teen EBITDA margins.
So even in the month of June, we could not ship out 30% of our goods which were ready due to non-availability of the ships and containers.
So, I think it's still continuing at 10% only at the moment. How it goes future is anyone's guess, Saurabh.
So basically, we have lot of structured programs in our manufacturing and supply chain operations.

Management was evasive on the sustainable margin path, repeatedly pointing to a full-year "high teens" view rather than quantifying the quarter's freight drag, and deflected questions on Soul and on the tariff rate outlook.

rows.why: Management is already executing Surat greenfield with Phase 2 lines and only INR20-25 crore residual capex in FY27, and utilisation of combined capacity is not stated as near full, so a fresh major capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.why: Shipments constrained by container and vessel shortages (about 30% of June ready goods unshipped), March was zero shipments in West Asia disruption, and FY27 revenue target is explicitly conditional on shipping conditions easing; the carry-forward could slip from Q2 into Q3.

rows.why: No new product, brand or molecule launches were discussed; Soul relaunch is described as still slow.

rows.why: Freight pass-through began in Q1 FY27 at about 75% in the US and 65-70% overall, offsetting about 3% of consolidated revenue freight cost, though tariff benefits will be passed back selectively to support share.

rows.why: Management described the order book as the strongest in company history for June, July and August, with Ashoka growing above 30% and Truly Indian in 3,000+ US stores.

rows.why: PLI was about INR16 crore in FY26 (about 2% of revenue) and FY27 is its final year; management only hopes for an extension, so the tailwind fades after FY27.

519397|2026-03.headline: Sharat Industries FY26 revenue rose about 38% to Rs 524.7 crore and PAT about 60% to Rs 15.90 crore, while Q4 was hit by Middle East disruption and fishmeal costs.
519397|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a strong year on revenue and profit, with export revenue up about 23% and export volumes up about 8%. Q4 revenue grew about 25% YoY to Rs 117.24 crore, but margins were squeezed by the West Asia conflict, which forced rerouting of Middle East-bound shipments, higher logistics costs and inventory build-up, along with sharp fishmeal and soya price increases. US tariffs on Indian shrimp fell from up to 50% to 10% effective February 2026, and management is targeting FY27-28 export revenue of up to Rs 1,000 crore. Management framed the Q4 margin pressure as largely external and event-driven rather than a change in the underlying business.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: US and China make up roughly 40% of export portfolio; Russia, Southeast Asia, Europe and Middle East the remaining 60%. Value-added products were about 7-10% of export volume in FY26, with management hoping to double that share by volume if conditions normalise.

segments.name: Domestic / feed and farming
segments.commentary: Q4 is the start of stocking season in Andhra Pradesh farming, but sharp fishmeal and soya price increases hurt margins. Feed market share is sub 2%. Sales to Hyperpure began in Q4 FY26 with base products such as raw frozen shrimp.

segments.name: Processing
segments.commentary: Premium black tiger shrimp and new value-added products are a stated priority. A 1 MW captive solar plant is partly commissioned in Q4, with the balance due shortly.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term roadmap to FY27-28 targets annual export revenue of up to Rs 1,000 crore, via deeper Russia and China penetration, re-entry into the EU and a measured domestic and value-added build-out.
US exports expected to scale up significantly versus the last couple of years in FY27, but management is cautious and will revisit clarity around end of the quarter.
Value-added share of export volume hoped to double from 7-10% if export conditions normalise.
EU FTA expected to take effect over the rest of calendar 2026; benefits to accrue gradually.
Raw material prices and realisations expected to keep moving through the cycle; management hopes the fishmeal spike is temporary.
capex_capacity: 1 MW solar plant for captive consumption at processing division: partly commissioned in Q4 FY26, balance to be commissioned shortly.
Insect protein substitution for fishmeal in feed: pilot farming under way for over a year, with farm-level results described as encouraging.
Management aims to improve processing plant utilisation and unlock operating leverage via contract farming and asset-light merchant exports; slight utilisation improvement was seen in FY26.
No quantified capacity, utilisation percentage or capex amount was given.
demand_pricing: About 20 containers were planned for Middle East shipments in Q4; about half were rerouted on customer advice, about five were in transit and needed rescue by shipping liners, and the rest are held as inventory being reprocessed for alternate destinations.
US tariffs on Indian shrimp cut from up to 50% to 10% effective February 2026; US is about 35-40% of export value. No new US clients were added in FY26 due to tariff turbulence.
Russia: two new clients added in FY26. China: new black tiger shrimp product, about five customers worked with so far.
PD Curl control product (launched in Russia) delivers incremental EBITDA margin of more than 5% up to about 10% over base EBITDA, but volumes are low.
Indian shrimp exports are about Rs 50,000-55,000 crore; company share is 0.5-0.75%.
Fishmeal price spike attributed to global demand and heavy Indian exports; industry has petitioned government for relief.

qa_highlights.question: How much business was hit by the West Asia conflict, and have deferred orders been recovered?
qa_highlights.answer: About 20 containers were planned for Middle East in Q4; half were rerouted to other destinations, about five were in transit and needed safe handling at extra cost, and the remainder sit in inventory being reprocessed for other markets.

qa_highlights.question: What are the key drivers of the ~60% PAT growth versus EBITDA growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited export diversification (China black tiger shrimp via a partner processor), slightly higher capacity utilisation, and value-added products improving margins; geopolitical shocks would otherwise have allowed better margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PD Curl control product's potential and where can it go next?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental EBITDA margin of more than 5% up to about 10% over base; volumes are currently low, and management plans to add products to the Russian portfolio this year.

qa_highlights.question: What are the company's market shares?
qa_highlights.answer: Share of Indian shrimp exports is about 0.5%, ranging 0.5-0.75%; feed market share is sub 2%, described as a minority position.

qa_highlights.question: What is the value-added share of exports and the FY27 plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Value-added products were about 7-10% of export volume in FY26; the company hopes to double that share by volume if export conditions are normal.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company handling the fishmeal price increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Insect protein substitution is in pilot; some costs passed to contract farmers; the company aims for better export contracts with improved margins; industry has sought government relief.

risks_watch: Fishmeal and soya cost inflation, which hit Q4 margins and may persist.
Middle East conflict: inventory of rerouted cargo must be sold through alternate channels; logistics costs elevated.
Weather-related farm risk flagged for the rest of calendar 2026.
US demand normalisation and recession risk; tariff level sustainability.
EU FTA ratification timing across member states; benefit may take time.
Q4 seasonal softness and whether margins recover in the next quarter.

519552|2026-03.headline: Heritage Foods Q4 FY26 revenue rose 10% YoY to INR 11,576 million, but EBITDA margin fell to 4.5% on procurement inflation of 8%.
519552|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 10% YoY to INR 11,576 million and FY26 revenue reached INR 45,260 million. Milk procurement cost rose 8% YoY to INR 46.67 per litre (landed at chilling centre) while procurement volume fell 7% to 16.38 lakh litres per day, squeezing EBITDA to INR 522 million (4.5% margin) and PAT to INR 230 million (2.1% margin). Value-added products (VAP) grew 18% YoY in Q4 and rose to 35.5% of revenue from 32.5%. Management said cow milk flush has started in key southern regions but surplus is not yet large enough to soften procurement prices.

financial_highlights.change: FY bulk fat revenue was about INR 125 crore last year (per management, approx. 70% decline)

financial_highlights.metric: Consumer fats (ghee and salted butter) revenue FY26

519552|2026-06.headline: Heritage Foods Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18% to INR13,381 million, but EBITDA margin fell to 4.6% as raw milk costs rose 7% YoY.
519552|2026-06.overview: Heritage posted its highest-ever quarterly revenue of INR13,381 million (+18% YoY), with EBITDA of INR619 million (4.6% margin) and PAT of INR150 million (1.9% margin). Value-added products (VAP) grew 40% YoY to INR5,636 million and reached 44% of consolidated revenue, while milk procurement cost rose 7% YoY to INR46.61/litre amid tight supply. Management attributed the margin squeeze to cow-milk price inflation, buffalo milk degrowth, higher SMP consumption and packaging costs, and said pricing actions are continuing into July. Liquid milk volume growth remains the main open problem.

segments.commentary: VAP revenue INR5,636 million (+40%), EBITDA margin 8.06% vs 9.7% last year. Volume contributed ~35pp of growth and price ~5.12%. Paneer +33%, curd +26%, butter milk +60%, lassi +98%.

segments.commentary: Ice cream crossed INR550 million (+65%); Alpenvie +44%; new facility at ~40% utilisation, producing both brands on a common platform. Ice cream is the highest-margin VAP per management.

segments.commentary: Revenue INR728 million (+37% YoY) with PBT of INR20 million despite elevated input costs.

519552|2026-09.headline: Heritage Foods Q2 FY27 revenue rose 19% to INR13,196 million, with EBITDA margin at 5.6%, up 98 bps QoQ despite milk procurement cost up 11% YoY.

EBITDA was INR740 million (5.6% margin), up 98 bps sequentially, while PAT was INR309 million. Landed milk procurement cost rose 11% YoY to INR47.73/litre, and management passed through about 8% weighted average price increase, with a larger hike taken in September that benefits Q3. Management expects further procurement inflation in Q3 and is watching the post-Diwali buffalo flush.

520057|2026-03.headline: JTEKT India FY26 sales grew 11% vs 9% PV market, but full-year EBITDA margin slipped to 7.5% from 7.6% on mix and forex.
520057|2026-03.overview: FY26 sales grew 11% against passenger vehicle market growth of 9%, helped by GST cuts and new Maruti Suzuki models (e Vitara, Victoris). Second-half EBITDA margin recovered to 8.48% from 7.71%, while H1 margin was 6.3%, leaving the full year at 7.5%. Management attributed the margin drag to product mix (Honda down about 33%, 0.33% impact), a forex accounting effect (0.23%) and US tariffs (0.24%), which it called largely temporary. New capacity (CVJ line 2, MS Gear line 5 and 6, CPS line 3) is still under-utilised, and management expects it to reach full utilisation over 1 to 1.5 years. A Brazil export order from the JTEKT group starts dispatch in May 2026.

segments.commentary: Maruti Suzuki rose to 60% of sales from 56%, Toyota fell to 10% from 12%, Honda fell to 5% from 8%, M&M and Tata stayed at 10%, exports rose to 3% from 2%.

segments.name: CVJ (driveline)
segments.commentary: FY26 sales about INR 130 crore per management; line 2 (from Nov 2025, capacity about 370,000 units) is 27% utilised, line 1 about 83%. Full two-line volume targeted at about INR 250 crore with the Maruti EV MPV from October 2026.

segments.name: Manual gear (MS Gear)
segments.commentary: Line 5 at Dharuhera is at 106% utilisation; line 6 is at 21%, expected to reach 60% then 80-90%. Company holds 40-45% share of manual gear business.

segments.name: CPS
segments.commentary: Line 3 at Bawal is about 50% utilised; capacity about 5 lakh units per line.

guidance_outlook: Management expects new capacity to be fully utilised within 1 to 1.5 years, depending on market conditions.

Illustrative FY27 incremental revenue: about INR 400 crore from 10% market growth plus INR 75-100 crore exports, so about INR 500 crore; management referred to INR 800 crore total extra business across FY26 and FY27 (INR 300 crore achieved in FY26). Management declined to give formal FY27 guidance.
Brazil (Stellantis) order to start dispatch in May 2026, about 70,000 units in FY27 (management cited 70,000 this year and 100,000-150,000 next year), with potential to reach 5 lakh units per year.
Honda's EV SUV from Tapukara expected around December 2026, optimistically about 40,000 units and about INR 100 crore business for JTEKT.

Management expects the margin pressures from product mix and forex accounting to be temporary; US tariff reduced from 50% to 10% after the Supreme Court ruling, which management expects to lift US exports.
Capex for FY27 expected to be lower than the last two years; about INR 100 crore more for the Gujarat plant (total committed about INR 250 crore, INR 130 crore spent), plus normal capex.
capex_capacity: CVJ line 2 commissioned November 2025; capacity about 7.54 lakh units per annum (about 3.8 lakh vehicle sets); line 2 utilisation 27%, line 1 about 83%; work started on a third CVJ line.
MS Gear line 5 at Dharuhera 106% utilised; MS Gear line 6 at 21%; MS Gear line 4 at Chennai for export not yet started (SOP pending); capacity about 3.5-4 lakh per MS Gear line.
CPS line 3 at Bawal about 50% utilised; capacity about 5 lakh units per line.
Chennai rack and pinion line for Brazil export with installed capacity about 4 lakh units.
Gujarat plant committed at about INR 250 crore; about INR 130 crore spent so far, and about INR 100 crore further spend expected over 1-2 years.
CWIP of about INR 411 crore; management asked analysts to track CWIP as it will weigh on ratios for 1-2 years.
demand_pricing: PV market grew 9% in FY26, with 16.7% growth in H2 after GST cut (28% to 18% for small cars; 50% to 40% for larger ones); H1 growth was only 1.6%.
Honda's passenger vehicle business fell about 30%, reducing JTEKT's sales (almost 100% supplier to Honda); Renault-Nissan export models fell about 16%, Toyota about 4%.
Raw material cost pass-through to customers is back-to-back with a time lag, per management.
Competition in CVJ from GKN-linked and other suppliers, which hold over 60% of Maruti's business; management targets at least 15% CVJ share.
Management said it is not supplying Renault's Duster.

qa_highlights.question: Why have gross margins declined from 29% to 27% over two years, and how should they trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 margin was 6.3% and H2 8.48%; net variable cost drag of 0.18% came from a 0.33% mix effect (Honda, Renault-Nissan, Toyota down; Maruti GST-driven models higher), 0.23% forex accounting effect and 0.24% US tariffs, offset by export gains and lower warranty. Management called these temporary.

qa_highlights.question: Has Toyota's Bidadi third line commenced, and what is Toyota's revenue share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Bidadi line had not commenced per its understanding; a new Maharashtra facility is expected in H1 FY29, lifting Toyota capacity to about 1 lakh vehicles. JTEKT is the only steering supplier to Toyota.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan for other driveline products beyond CVJ and hub bearings for JTEKT's group?
qa_highlights.answer: No concrete plan is finalised; management said it needs 1-1.5 years to stabilise CVJ first. It noted export opportunities for CVJ parts to group entities.

qa_highlights.question: Update on the INR 1,000 crore top-line addition by FY27 and whether revenue can double in 3-4 years.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR 300 crore was added in FY26; with 10% market growth and INR 75-100 crore exports, about INR 500 crore more is possible in FY27 (about INR 800 crore total). It declined to share a formal business plan and said growth depends on the market.

qa_highlights.question: Expected FY27 capex and ROCE trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex will be lower than the last two years, with about INR 100 crore for Gujarat plus normal capex. ROCE excluding CWIP is above 11%, and full utilisation should push it back toward earlier levels (about 16-17%).

qa_highlights.question: Driveline pipeline, CVJ margins and fixed asset turnover?
qa_highlights.answer: CVJ margins are better than most MS Gear products and it is 100% localised. Target fixed asset turnover is about 3x overall; CVJ is lower (about 1.5x), CPS 2.5-3x, manual gear 2-2.5x.

qa_highlights.question: Potential for exports to US and Europe?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Brazil is the first step, with a Stellantis order, and that a further order could follow once quality and cost are established. No firm US or Europe plan was given.

Rising state power tariffs and reciprocal tariffs on US exports.

522074|2026-06.headline: Elgi Q1 FY27 revenue grew about 23% (7 points from exchange), EBITDA up 28%, with EBITDA margin held flat year on year at prior-year level.
522074|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue growth of about 23%, of which about 7 points were exchange-related, with growth across all geographies. EBITDA grew about 28% and EBITDA margin was maintained at last year's level despite raw material inflation, tariffs and adverse product mix. PAT margin was about 9.7%, roughly flat YoY, after exceptional reorganisation costs in Australia, Europe and the US. Management said price corrections to offset metal cost inflation would take effect towards the end of Q2 and more fully in Q3, so the Q1 margin does not yet reflect them.

financial_highlights.value: Maintained at prior-year level, management said slightly better
Up about 12%, mainly rental premises for motor plant and US facilities sold and leased back
About 1.6-1.8 million of approx. 4 million approved; balance pending

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Grew about 28%, described as primarily volume-driven, with growth across industrial, portables, aftermarket and vacuum. Growth cited in EV ecosystem, renewables and semiconductor supply chains; water well segment picked up in the quarter.

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: Grew about 37%. Distribution business underperformed, mainly on service side; other businesses performed well.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Grew about 21%. Run as a P&L play now, targeted at breakeven; plans to enter Germany and expand in Eastern Europe, with tighter cost control.

segments.name: Australia
segments.commentary: Grew about 17% but described as muted; service and distribution operations being reset, with recovery expected by Q3-Q4.

segments.name: Southeast Asia
segments.commentary: Described as a challenge for an Indian brand; not a significant contributor; longer-term play.

segments.name: Vacuum (Italian JV product)
segments.commentary: Locally produced and selling since indigenisation; management described Q1 growth as phenomenal in percentage terms from a small base, with no figure given.

Management expects EBITDA margin to keep improving, citing operating leverage, product launches, constant cost reduction and fixed cost rationalisation over 3-4 years.
Medium-term EBITDA margin target of 20%; prior guidance of 18% by 2031 was mentioned in Q&A.
Tier 4 entry-level compressor range to launch formally in September 2026 (Hyderabad exhibition); first orders already received; marginal contribution to top line this year.
Demand=Match to be introduced in rest-of-world models during 2026; management expects all products to carry it within about a year.
Some reorganisation costs in Australia, Europe and the US expected to continue into the year.
capex_capacity: Capex mainly for MK2, the programme to shift the campus from the city factory to a new campus; about half of capex.
Land purchased in Italy under a commitment made six years earlier, plus routine factory equipment.
Motor plant moved to rented premises; US facilities sold and replaced with rental facilities.
Insourced motor manufacturing cited as a significant cost-saving driver.
demand_pricing: Inquiry levels described as very strong, though deal finalisation timelines are longer than normal.
Price correction only marginal in Q1; growth described as primarily volume-driven.
Demand=Match technology, launched September 2025, is embedded in tier 1-3 models as standard and cited as a key driver of new-customer wins in India.
Aftermarket parts are about 28-30% of India revenue and about 15-16% globally (parts only); management said global service benchmark is about 38%.
Warranty cost stated as below 1% of revenue; management said competitors are higher, though not publicly reported.
Steel sector capacity utilisation weak; management said steel is bleeding capacity utilisation before new investment.

qa_highlights.question: How much of India's 28% growth was volume versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: Primarily volume-driven, with only a marginal price correction in Q1; raw material costs rose 5-6% versus the 3% planned, and management expects to recover this in later quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is Elgi gaining Indian market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it thinks so but would prefer competitors confirm it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the aftermarket share of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Parts are about 20-23% of group revenue, about 28-30% in India and about 15-16% in the rest of the world; service is a small part in India and is left largely to dealers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the warranty cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Less than 1% of revenue; competitors are believed to be higher than 1%, though not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What drove margin improvement in international subsidiaries?
qa_highlights.answer: North America growth, restructuring to lean the organisation, cost reduction including in-house motor manufacturing, and price holding in Q1, with price corrections expected to add from Q2-Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Will employee and operating costs rationalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost ratios should fall as revenue grows; a process-layer project over 3-4 years is expected to identify lower-cost locations for specific jobs.

Raw material inflation: management said price corrections lag cost inflation, so Q2 margins could be pressured before recovery.
Australia service and distribution reset and Southeast Asia challenges.
Reorganisation costs expected to continue into the year, which may keep PAT margin under pressure.

Tier 4 launch in a segment where low-cost Chinese compressors compete on price.

522101|2026-03.headline: Kilburn Q4 FY26 standalone revenue INR134 crores at 25.1% EBITDA; FY27 guidance 20-25% growth to INR750-800 crores with order intake target INR800-1,000 crores.
522101|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 standalone revenue of INR134 crores with 25.1% EBITDA margin and FY26 standalone revenue of INR448 crores at 25.9%. Consolidated FY26 revenue was INR629 crores at 25.13% EBITDA, with Q4 consolidated revenue of INR189 crores at 22.95%, the latter diluted by freight and subcontract costs on a large Moroccan order. Working capital days rose from 169 to 184 and operating cash flow was negative on a standalone basis, which management attributed to heavy dispatches in the last two months of the year. Several large orders slipped by about a quarter due to the Middle East crisis, and the Monga Strayfield dispatches were delayed by logistics constraints.

segments.name: Kilburn Engineering (standalone)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR134 crores at 25.1% EBITDA; standalone trade receivables rose by about INR100 crores in FY26 as Q4 dispatches reached about INR130 crores versus INR50-60 crores a year earlier. Expansion at Saravali plant expected by end Q2 FY27.

segments.name: M.E. Energy (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Phase 2 expansion at Pune expected by end Q2 FY27. Strong ferrous alloy and steel inquiries; cement business mainly hot air generators with repeat orders; first waste heat recovery boiler inquiry in cement at early stage. Quoting jobs above INR300 crores.

segments.name: Monga Strayfield (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue hit by Middle East logistics disruption; ready equipment held in storage awaiting shipping. Management expects catch-up by first half FY27. Revenue split approximately 50:50 between RF dryers and sheet metal, per management range guidance. Short order cycle of about 3 months.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth target 20-25%, implying INR750-800 crores at group level; target to reach INR1,000 crores by FY28.
FY27 group order intake target INR800-1,000 crores; management expects at least INR450-500 crores closed by end Q2 FY27 and INR500-600 crores booked by September.
EBITDA margin guidance 20%+ with management referencing a 22-23% operating range; management said other income (about 80% operating, mainly export FX gains) should be included in EBITDA.
Depreciation expected at INR14-15 crores, rising by a few crores after new capex; finance cost expected to stay broadly stable.
Capex for FY27 around INR40 crores, spread across standalone and subsidiaries; capex programme expected complete by Sept-Oct 2026.
Management sees exports reaching 30-40% of revenue over time.
capex_capacity: Kilburn Saravali factory expansion and M.E. Energy Phase 2 expansion at Pune both expected by end Q2 FY27.
Management says capacity after current expansion is sufficient for INR800 crores of revenue comfortably; further capex needed for growth to FY28 scale.
Office building demolished to make way for a new bay at the factory; INR2-3 crores written off in opex.
Capex programme under implementation expected to complete September-October 2026.
demand_pricing: Inquiry pipeline about INR4,000 crores at consolidated level across fertilizer, nuclear, sludge processing, petrochemicals, offshore gas vapour recovery, steel and ferrous alloy, cement, textiles, food processing and defrosting.
Two nuclear orders in hand, expected to take a year plus to execute; competition mainly from Lloyds Engineering; 2-3 further nuclear projects visible (including Kaiga), via EPC partners.
Several orders expected to close in Q4 FY26 slipped by about a quarter due to Middle East crisis; a Moroccan order of INR50-60 crores receivable in the next 2-3 months.
Material costs rising with steel prices; management says material is booked at order award and cost is not passed through, though prices rise with turnover.
Inquiry ticket sizes: INR2-5 crores for smaller machines, about INR40 crores for some inquiries, and INR100 crores+ for large projects; tea dryers INR40-50 lakhs excluded.

qa_highlights.question: Why has standalone cash flow turned negative and when will operating cash flow turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Vijayakar attributed it to receivables from heavy Q4 dispatches (about INR130 crores versus INR50-60 crores a year earlier); collections expected from June. Consolidated operating cash flow is positive. Working capital days to reduce, but not drastically.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating leverage not show in FY26 and why has PAT lagged revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Amritanshu Khaitan said leverage has already been achieved and margins are stable at about 25%; growth is being reinvested in people, talent and infrastructure. PAT lag reflects full tax from FY26 versus carried-forward losses earlier, plus the INR2-3 crore write-off.

qa_highlights.question: Has the FY27 growth guidance been cut from 25-30% to 20-25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Khaitan said the guidance has always been 20-25% and was not changed; the 25-30% figure in the investor presentation was a typo by the IR team, with the press release showing 20-25%.

qa_highlights.question: Is any further warrant-related dilution expected?
qa_highlights.answer: All warrant conversions have happened; no further dilution expected.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin decline in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Vijayakar said the executing orders had a higher share of outside subcontract charges; margin depends on order mix and equipment type.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management of INR750-800 crores revenue given a tepid opening order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Ranjit Lala said some orders slipped by a quarter and management will revert next quarter if there is deviation; Khaitan said H2 will carry more of the execution weight, assuming orders are finalised in 30-60 days.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be a sector or subsidiary breakup of order intake?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a subsidiary or sector order breakup, citing that orders can be executed across plants.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margins recover to 23-25% in FY27-28 with steel prices normalising?
qa_highlights.answer: Khaitan said other income should be included in margin (about 80% operating); quarterly margin is about 23% and full-year consolidated is 25%. Ranjit Lala said costs are not passed through and the normal target range is 20-23%, with 25% possibly not sustainable every year.

risks_watch: Order intake timing: management expects INR450-500 crores closed by end Q2 FY27, against an opening backlog of INR467 crores that management concedes is lower than last year.

Working capital and receivables: standalone receivables rose by about INR100 crores; management expects collections of about INR50-60 crores from the Moroccan order and recovery from June to September.
Middle East crisis effects on shipping lead times, gas availability for production and Monga Strayfield dispatches.
Steel and metal price inflation with no pass-through clause; management books material at order award.
Guidance messaging: the investor presentation showed a 25-30% CAGR typo versus 20-25% in the press release; the IR team should correct the document.

522101|2026-06.headline: Kilburn Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell to about INR117 crores with 20.1% EBITDA margin; FY27 guidance of INR700 crores kept, H2-weighted.
522101|2026-06.overview: Consolidated Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was about INR117 crores, with EBITDA of INR24.2 crores (20.1% margin), which management called below the level it had targeted. Management attributed the shortfall to customer-driven timing: delayed approvals of drawings and inspections, deferred project executions, and longer decision cycles linked to geopolitical conditions. Management kept FY27 guidance of about INR700 crores revenue at 20% EBITDA margin and said the year is expected to be significantly second-half weighted. Order inflow was about INR134-135 crores in the quarter and about INR190 crores year-to-date, against an internal group target of INR800 crores for FY27. Management also said the equity fundraise is complete and the balance sheet is net debt-free.

Closing order book (as cited in Q&A)
financial_highlights.change: Analyst cited INR467 crores for prior quarter; not confirmed by management

financial_highlights.value: approx. INR98 crores subscription money received in the quarter, shares allotted at INR425

segments.name: Kilburn Engineering (standalone)
segments.commentary: Management said standalone performance was relatively weak this quarter; drying solutions inquiries expected to close by end Q1/early Q2, carbon black jobs on hold pending environmental and land clearances. Nuclear jobs (NPCIL, Heavy Water Board) face longer approvals than fertilizer jobs (Casale).

segments.name: M.E. Energy (waste heat recovery)
segments.commentary: Entering ferrous alloy via a Bhutan project; multiple ferrous alloy and cement inquiries; steel-sector inquiries in the INR10-15 crore size range. Capacity expansion at Kilburn and M.E. Energy expected to complete by end October 2026.

segments.commentary: Expanding metal sheet fabrication capacity for data-center storage equipment; details to be disclosed over time. Developing new drying-sector products.

qa_highlights.question: Use of the INR98 crore fundraise proceeds and whether further fundraising is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Amritanshu Khaitan said proceeds strengthen the balance sheet (net debt-free) and partly fund capex to support over INR1,000 crores revenue; acquisitions are being evaluated but none announced; no further fundraise needed.

qa_highlights.question: Confidence in reaching INR800 crore order inflow with 9 months left, and Middle East exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited INR4,000 crore inquiry pipeline and fertilizer traction; no current Middle East orders, but a couple of large inquiries were at final commercial stage before the conflict, now on hold.

qa_highlights.question: Why revenue growth ambition of about 25% has slipped to about 10-12% and what is being done differently?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited customer-side dependencies, nuclear approvals taking longer than private jobs, and greenfield projects held by environmental clearances; no FY28 guidance until order booking through March 2027 is clearer.

qa_highlights.question: Is margin pressure linked to Kilburn standalone weakness?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Vijayakar said the company has consistently maintained 20%+ margins on a consolidated basis, citing cost and execution discipline, and reports consolidated because of cross-selling.

qa_highlights.question: Operating cash flow and working capital status?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Vijayakar said collections were received after March; debtors and net working capital have not changed substantially but are better than the March quarter.

qa_highlights.answer: Ranjit Lala said it is a SEBI LODR disclosure requirement for reporting lines one level below the CEO after recent promotions; no board induction planned.

522113|2026-03.headline: Timken India Q4 FY26 revenue crossed INR1,000 crore for first time, up 14.2% YoY to INR10,731 million; PBT margin 19.3%.
522113|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue from operations was INR10,731 million (up 14.2% YoY), the first quarter above INR1,000 crore, with PBT of INR2,074 million (19.3% margin) after a labour code impact. FY26 standalone revenue hit a record INR31,478 million (up 8.6%), with PBT of INR5,304 million (up about 3%) and PBT margin of 15.5%. The Board approved merging Timken GGB into Timken India. Management flagged input cost inflation entering FY27, with price pass-through only about 10% achieved so far, and said the new Bharuch plant is ramping slowly with about INR80 crore of FY26 revenue.

Price increases to offset raw material inflation (steel, grinding wheels, coolants, currency): about 10% achieved as of the call, with the aim of completing most of the pass-through over the current and next quarter.
Bharuch CRB/SRB plant expected to reach about 70% utilisation by July-August 2026, improving monthly after that.
Jamshedpur rail expansion (about INR120 crore capex): first production targeted for November-December 2026, with asset turns of about 2x to start.
FY27 capex expected at about 8-10% of revenue (management pegged last two years at about 8.5%), covering Jamshedpur rail, GGB plain bearings at Bharuch and some heat-treatment investment.
Management said the 65:35 domestic-manufactured to imported mix may hold for the next 2-3 years.
capex_capacity: Bharuch new plant: all lines capitalised; smaller lines and spherical lines running near full, large-line PPAPs under way, and CRB lines running close to two shifts. More than 100 new part introductions underway. FY26 revenue from the plant about INR80 crore (Q4 about INR60 crore, Q3 about INR12 crore). Management said the plant is still close to breakeven.

Bharuch total investment about INR720 crore including forex; buildings about INR350 crore; plant and machinery roughly INR310-320 crore by management's estimate. Peak revenue said to be close to 2x asset turns, but management ruled out INR1,000 crore.
Jamshedpur rail expansion: about INR120 crore capex, imported robotic machines from Europe, all approvals in place. Management said the building was built with spare capacity.
Plain bearing expansion at Bharuch and renewable energy investments are progressing; management said both are broadly on track.
Capital is debt-free; management said it will consider further expansion (0-8 inch range for CV and tractors, M&A) if the project is right.
demand_pricing: Management said demand is stable across most segments and is not among its top three concerns; cost escalation and pass-through, Bharuch ramp-up/PPAP, and expansion projects are the top three.
Steel MRO is slow and steel melt was lower in the quarter; cement MRO is good. OE sentiment is wait-and-watch because of geopolitics.
North America export demand is gaining momentum even without a signed US trade deal; the US is about 50% of exports, per the analyst.
CV demand described as robust with cyclicality; tractors okay; rail slow and steady; aftermarket okay.
Pricing: price increases began mid-April 2026 for both pass-through and recovery; about 10% realised, with automotive customers expected to delay. Management hopes for retrospective recovery.
Management said the Indian bearing market is about USD 2-2.5 billion (about 65% mobile, 35% stationary) and expects process and distribution to grow fastest.

522113|2026-06.headline: Timken India Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~15% YoY to INR929 crore, with PBT of INR150 crore and PBT margin of 16.2%.
522113|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR929 crore, up almost 15% YoY, after a seasonally strong Q4 FY26 (highest standalone revenue of INR3,147 crore for FY26). PBT rose to INR150 crore from INR130 crore, with PBT margin at 16.2% versus 16.1% a year earlier, and EBITDA margin at 19.6%. Gross margin was 39.9%, up 100 bps YoY and roughly flat QoQ, which management attributed to heavy-truck and off-highway price increases offsetting unfavourable Q1 mix. The Bharuch plant is ramping up quickly, with revenue of about INR50 crore in the quarter and near breakeven.

segments.name: Rail
segments.commentary: INR200 crore, about 22% of Q1 revenue. Management described government railway buying as slow and sluggish, and said the year started with about 3% growth in rail.

segments.name: Mobile / others
segments.commentary: INR184 crore. Management said mobile (tractors, heavy trucks) is about 20% of the business and is where price increases are sticking.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: INR153.9 crore (about INR154 crore).

segments.name: Process
segments.commentary: INR186 crore, up about 28-30% YoY, driven by metals customers and wind (gearbox exports and domestic wind farms).

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: About INR200 crore, including about 1% export incentive. Intercompany push to America rose about 21%; Europe is down, China and ASEAN are down, and the US is up.

segments.name: Bharuch plant (within segments)
segments.commentary: About INR50 crore revenue in Q1, close to breakeven. Spherical roller bearing (SRB) line utilisation was about 40-45% in Q1, targeted at about 70% by August-September; CRB line utilisation is lower, with ramp toward Q2-end and Q3.

guidance_outlook: Bharuch SRB line expected to reach about 70% utilisation in August-September 2026; CRB line ramp toward end of Q2 and Q3.
Rail expansion at Jamshedpur expected to start commercial production by calendar year-end 2026; management said it will ramp up immediately after that.
FY27 capex expected at about 8-10% of sales, with project work described as on track; timing may spill some capex into FY28.
Further cost escalation seen as limited beyond the steel, carbide, coal and grinding increases already in the system; base oil described as the only volatile input.
Management said it will continue to pass on cost increases to heavy-truck and off-highway customers as contracts renew; rail and PSU/ARC contracts are fixed and will reprice only at renewal.
capex_capacity: Bharuch plant ramping up; three manufacturing lines; utilisation cannot be given at plant level but SRB demand is higher than CRB at this stage.
Rail investment at Jamshedpur on track; plain bearings investment at Bharuch on track.
Manufactured vs traded mix roughly 75/25, similar to prior quarters.
Gas conversion from LPG to natural gas completed across supply chain and plants.
demand_pricing: Revenue growth driven by resilient core-segment demand and both export and domestic execution.
Steel producers raised prices by about INR1,500-1,600 per tonne in January and about INR3,500 per tonne by April, around INR5,000 per tonne in total; most customers have started paying the increase.
Price pass-through is working in heavy truck and tractor/off-highway; rail, PSU and cement customers are on fixed annual rate contracts.
Process growth partly from metals projects (mills built in India for export) and wind.
Management said the US market is up, Europe and China are down, and ASEAN and Australia are flat to down.
No direct tariff figure given; management said the US landed tariff has moved over time and it would confirm the current rate.
Management said the parent's 80/20 portfolio review is aimed at performance improvement; no change in Indian strategy was announced.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue split for Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Rail INR200 crore (22%), mobile/others INR184 crore, distribution INR153.9 crore, process INR186 crore, exports about INR200 crore including 1% export incentive.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of parent's 80/20 strategy and belts divestment on India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 80/20 is a Pareto-based performance tool that is being applied globally; it is not yet a change in strategy for India. The India focus stays on off-highway, rail and tractor/heavy-truck, with no two-wheeler, passenger car or washing-machine ball bearings.

qa_highlights.question: Bharuch ramp-up and utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 Bharuch revenue was about INR50 crore, close to breakeven. SRB utilisation was about 40-45% in Q1, expected to reach about 70% by August-September; CRB is lower with ramp toward Q2-end and Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of process and export growth and US outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Process grew about 30% YoY, from metals and wind. Exports to the US are growing, Europe is down, and the intercompany push to America is about 21%.

qa_highlights.question: Rail outlook and Jamshedpur ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Government railway procurement is slow due to funds diverted to infrastructure and defence; management expects this to be timing-related. Jamshedpur rail capacity is due to start commercial production by calendar year-end.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the cost inflation has been passed through to price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is hard to give an exact percentage; heavy truck and tractor customers have largely passed through cost escalation, while rail and PSU contracts will reprice at renewal.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 capex plan and allocation?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant-wise split not given; capex directionally in line with the 8-10% of sales range, with some timing spillover into the next fiscal.

risks_watch: Steel and other input cost inflation: about INR5,000 per tonne of steel price increases; pass-through is incomplete for rail and PSU contracts that are fixed until renewal.
Slow government railway procurement due to fund diversion to infrastructure and defence; it could delay the Jamshedpur ramp-up benefit.
Bharuch ramp-up needs to reach about 70% SRB utilisation by August-September and CRB later; any slippage would weigh on margins.
Parent's 80/20 review and divestments (belts, automotive OE): the Indian implications are unclear, and management said it will review which assets can be used for growth in India.
Export exposure to geopolitics; Europe, China and ASEAN are down; US tariff status was not confirmed on the call.
Base oil price volatility affecting grease costs; the Brent outlook and the Middle East conflict affect energy and gas costs.
NCLT approval of the Timken GGB Technology merger is pending.
key_quotes: We have delivered high double-digit revenue growth this quarter Y-o-Y, driven by resilient demand, especially in the core segments, and our execution both for export and domestic.
So, the revenues are growing with every passing week, and I will ask Sujit to add more colour to the whole thing so that you get a little bit more specific answer.
So railway is a little bit sluggish as we speak, but it is an issue of time, so it will come back.
It is tough to tell you exactly percentage. Different customers, different behaviour.

rows.why: Steel rose about INR5,000 per tonne in total and management said it will keep passing cost increases to heavy-truck and off-highway customers as contracts renew, with most customers already paying.

522113|2026-09.headline: Timken India Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 25.4% YoY to INR 969 crore, with PBT up 29.5% to INR 156 crore and PBT margin at 16.1%.

Margins improved despite higher depreciation from new vessels, fuel and gas costs. The new Bharuch plant is ramping up, with SRB lines at 70% utilisation and CRB lines below 60%, and revenue from the plant at about INR 75 crore. Ethanol-to-SAF detailed engineering order from an international customer, following a completed basic engineering order last quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Margin trajectory over the next decade and service mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no margin guidance. It said services margins are higher than project margins and the mix shift (domestic/international, services/projects, new biofuels) is the route to better margins. Current investments in GenX, R&D and new ventures are absorbing margin.

qa_highlights.question: Bio-isobutanol mandate timing and biomaterials (bio-bitumen, PLA)?

Order intake fell to INR 7.15 billion in the quarter, and management said Greenfield ethanol projects in India are stalled by customer funding gaps and feedstock restrictions. Management pointed to CBG, international bioenergy, GenX data-centre and precision-fabrication work as the sources of H2 order growth.

522249|2026-03.headline: Mayur Uniquoters Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 22% to INR 260.55 crore and PAT 73% to INR 60.71 crore, helped by export mix and FX gains.

Shipping costs roughly quadrupled, and the company did not take a price increase on export OEM business, partly offset by about a 10% natural hedge from dollar appreciation.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 25% growth came from volume versus realisation?

qa_highlights.question: Why did margin fall sequentially from the previous quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the previous quarter was abnormally high due to a one-time forex gain; the sustainable margin is about 25% plus or minus 1-2%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the INR9 crore rise in other expenses QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Mixed: higher export shipping/freight, travel, legal and professional, and risk coverage costs. Management said some of this will continue and some will ease; part relates to the subsidiary.

522275|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 order intake of INR86.1bn (+188% YoY) lifted backlog to INR214.6bn; Q4 EBITDA margin hit a record 27.2%.
522275|2026-03.overview: GE Vernova T&D India reported a strong Q4 and full FY26, with revenue up 42% YoY in Q4 to INR16.4bn and 45% for the year to INR62.1bn. Profit before tax and exceptional items for FY26 rose to INR17.1bn from INR8.2bn, and the company ended the year with zero debt and about INR25bn of cash. Order intake was lifted by a large HVDC turnkey order from Adani Energy (VSC technology), and management guided to a mid-20s EBITDA margin for FY27. Management also announced a INR550mn disconnector and drives capacity at Vallam, Tamil Nadu, and a INR10 per share dividend.

segments.name: Domestic vs export
segments.commentary: Export orders in FY26 were about INR12bn versus INR32bn in FY25, which included one large export order; excluding large orders, base export orders grew 15-20%. Export was about 30% of FY25 revenue and new orders were about 92% domestic.

segments.name: Customer mix
segments.commentary: Backlog is 98% private customers, central utilities and PSUs; state utility exposure is under 2%.

segments.name: HVDC and projects
segments.commentary: A large HVDC turnkey order (Adani Energy, VSC) was booked in Q4, with execution mainly from FY28-29 onwards. Management does not disclose project versus product split.

guidance_outlook: Management endeavours to deliver mid-20s EBITDA margin going forward, after earlier guiding to low-20s and then mid-20s/high-20s in FY26.
Base order inflow expected to be around INR70bn (INR7,000 crore) and management remains confident of achieving it.
Two pending export RPT orders: a large export order where the decision is expected in H2 FY27, and a U.S. data-centre high-voltage order (about INR14-15bn) expected to be decided in Q1 FY27.
U.K. Grid Solutions purchase order (intra-group, feeding the Adani HVDC project) expected to be placed in the current quarter; it will not appear in the company's order book.
Capex of more than INR10bn to be phased from early FY27 through FY28, self-funded.
Management declined to give a split of Adani HVDC execution in early years; it said first two years would be lower than 30% and mostly engineering and supply-chain work.
capex_capacity: More than INR10bn of capex initiated across multiple product lines and facilities, to be phased through 2028.

INR550mn approved by the Board for new disconnector and drives capacity at Vallam, Tamil Nadu; disconnectors are being restarted for the Indian market, and some products will be global feeder factory output.
Air core reactor facility and HVDC thyristor valves and controls facility planned in India to raise local content.
Management did not give a revenue ballpark for the expanded capacity, citing that HVDC revenue depends on bought-out equipment and manpower rather than in-house capacity.
demand_pricing: Management says the TBCB pipeline has about 33 packages bid out, 21 of them at 765 kV; the only live HVDC tender is Barmer, whose bid deadline is being extended.
Data centres in India are about 1.5 GW installed, mostly at 220 kV; management expects a meaningful contribution once 400 kV and 765 kV data centres scale.
Transformer contracts carry price escalation clauses; for other products, cost inflation is built into tender pricing.
Management said Q4 domestic order finalisation was slightly dull, which it described as a conscious decision.

qa_highlights.question: Are export orders weak after FY25, and how will the RPT approvals translate into orders in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said excluding one large FY25 order, base export orders grew 15-20%. The pending RPT orders are a large export order (decision in H2 FY27), a U.S. data-centre order of about INR14-15bn (decision expected in Q1 FY27), and a U.K. Grid Solutions purchase order (intra-group).

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for FY27 and what was the INR50mn Q4 other expense item?
qa_highlights.answer: Management maintains an endeavour toward mid-20s EBITDA margin. The Q4 other expenses included about INR500mn of notional mark-to-market loss on foreign currency derivatives; management agreed EBITDA would have been better without it.

qa_highlights.question: Is Prolec's U.S. low-voltage distribution strategy relevant to the Indian entity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said India has no distribution-transformer manufacturing set-up, and entering would need organic or inorganic capacity; it said it does not see that as a current strategy.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Adani HVDC execution profile and the Barmer/South Kalamb project share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said early-year execution would be lower than 30%, with most revenue from FY29. For Barmer-type projects, the supplier share depends on line length and scope, not a fixed rule of thumb.

qa_highlights.question: Will HVDC refurbishment projects move from LCC to VSC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said LCC-to-LCC refurbishment only requires valves and controls changes, whereas LCC-to-VSC is a wider scope with higher shutdown requirement and capex; it depends on customer choice.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company likely to sustain high margins and growth for longer?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cycle is broader this time, covering the U.S., Europe, Middle East and Australia, and that export exposure is meaningful; it did not give a timeline for margin moderation.

risks_watch: Customer decision delays on large export RPT orders (H2 FY27 for one, Q1 FY27 for the U.S. order) and their conversion to revenue.
HVDC pipeline timing: Barmer bid deadline keeps being extended, and the next project after Barmer is not clearly scheduled.
Execution of the Adani HVDC turnkey order depends on securing a supply chain, with revenue weighted to FY29 onwards.
Imports of HVDC components (thyristor valves, controls hardware) remain, so local content is still limited until the new facility comes up.
Foreign-exchange derivative mark-to-market charges can affect other expenses and quarterly EBITDA.
522275|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on demand, backlog and margins, but cautious on timing: management repeatedly declined to give quantified guidance on HVDC phasing, pipeline timing and export mix, and said quarterly order intake can be lumpy.
key_quotes: So, yes, we remain confident on achieving the base order number of INR7,000 crores.
Our order book remained strong in Q4, and we saw a booking of INR86.1 billion, up by 188% year-on-year compared to INR29.9 billion in quarter ended March '25.
During the fourth quarter, we achieved a record EBITDA margin of 27.2%.
So, this time, the cycle is different. The market is different and the longevity of the cycle looks to be more sustainable.

522275|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 38% YoY to INR18.4 billion, but order intake fell 30% to INR11.4 billion and gross margin slipped to 41.3%.
522275|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 38% YoY to INR18.4 billion and PBT rose to INR4.9 billion, with EBITDA margin at 25.1%, within the mid-20s guided band. Order intake fell 30% YoY to INR11.4 billion, mainly on weak TBCB realisations in Jan-Mar 2026, so backlog eased 2.5% QoQ to INR209.3 billion. Gross margin fell to 41.3% from 45.3% in FY26, which management attributed to lower export mix, lower execution savings on elevated commodity prices, and HV business ramp-up. Two large related-party (RPT) orders, INR3,000 crore and INR1,300 crore, were delayed or on hold, and the company still has no firm plan for surplus cash of about INR16 billion beyond announced uses.

segments.commentary: Third-party orders about INR6.5 billion in Q1, per management. Private customers are 77% of backlog, central utilities and PSUs 21%, state utilities 2%.

segments.name: HVDC
segments.commentary: Backlog is back-ended; meaningful growth expected from FY29 onward. Developers' first-phase bids for the next HVDC projects are expected to be decided in August or September 2026.

Management stated it remains confident of the INR7,000-8,000 crore annual base order flow guidance, although Q1 base orders were about INR1,100 crore.
Domestic TBCB market expected flat or up 6-7% in FY27; double-digit growth not expected.

Capex on existing plants said to be tracking on schedule; management says it will not affect capacity utilisation.
Utilisation: some factories heavily loaded, others have room to grow.
demand_pricing: Q1 order intake down 30% YoY on weak TBCB realisations in Jan-Mar 2026; management says June-July TBCB pipeline is better, but the timing of conversion into orders is uncertain.

INR3,000 crore RPT order (a transformer project in the US per the call, though Q&A is unclear on the location) is on hold at the customer; approval lapses at the September AGM and would need re-validation. Management said it is not lost.
INR1,300 crore US data-centre RPT order not booked; expected in Q2 or Q3 FY27 after location and state change.
Data-centre orders are not significant in the current book; larger high-voltage data-centre projects are under discussion.

Commodity pass-through: transformers and HVDC carry IEEMA-linked escalation formulas; other turnkey work (CRGO and similar) is priced on forecast commodity costs with an 18-24 month order-to-execution lag.
Competition: Chinese GIS players approved; Tier-2 competition is limited in GIS and circuit breakers but present in other products.

qa_highlights.question: Are the INR3,000 crore and INR1,300 crore RPT orders being booked, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: None of the INR1,300 crore order is booked; it is expected in Q2 or Q3 FY27. The INR3,000 crore project is on hold at the customer over budget issues and would need fresh shareholder approval after the September AGM. Management said both are not lost.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there a jump in export orders, and what is the RPT pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Export pipeline improved on US utility demand for instrument transformers and 400 kV GIS opportunities. Management declined to comment on the new RPT pipeline beyond saying it will go to shareholders when projects become live.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin bridge from 45.3% FY26 gross margin to 41.3% in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: About 2-2.5 points from ramp-up of lower-margin HV business (offset at EBITDA level); 1-1.5 points from lower export share and a high-margin export order in FY26; and the rest from lower execution savings due to elevated commodity prices. EBITDA was 25.1%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the mid-20s EBITDA guidance intact, and how are commodity costs passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Mid-20s EBITDA guidance for FY27 is maintained. Transformers have formula-based escalation; other turnkey work relies on forecast costs, so cost pressure shows up in execution 1-2 years out.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Power Grid TBCB timeline stretching to 24-30 months a problem?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not affect capacity utilisation; ordering cycles may lengthen by about 3-4 months for longer tenders.

qa_highlights.question: What will the company do with surplus cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said options are under evaluation and nothing is firm; announced uses are INR10 billion capex and INR2.5 billion dividend, leaving about INR16 billion unallocated.

Surplus cash of about INR16 billion is unallocated; capital allocation decision still pending.

522275|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 32% YoY to INR20.3 billion and EBITDA margin hit 27.1%, the top of the mid-20s guidance band, with net zero debt.
522275|2026-09.overview: GE Vernova T&D India reported Q2 FY27 revenue of INR20.3 billion, up 32% YoY, with H1 revenue of INR38.6 billion, up 35%. Q2 order intake was INR24.4 billion, up 52% YoY, taking H1 intake to about INR35.8 billion (up 11%), and order backlog ended at INR214.4 billion. EBITDA was INR5.5 billion (27.1% of revenue) and PAT was INR4.3 billion (21.3%), with cash and equivalents of about INR32.5 billion. Management reiterated mid-20s EBITDA guidance for the full year and said HVDC execution will mostly start from FY28, while two related-party export orders are on hold or pending.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export share was 21% of Q2 orders and 32% of Q2 revenue; H1 export share was 29% of orders and 31% of revenue. Management says export orders carry higher margin than domestic, by about 500 bps as previously indicated.

522295|2026-03.headline: Control Print FY26 consolidated operating revenue rose to INR482 crores from INR425 crores; CP Italy (V-Shapes) packaging losses remain the key concern.
522295|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated total revenue of INR484 crores (vs INR431 crores) and standalone Q4 total revenue of about INR138 crores (vs INR114 crores). Standalone coding and marking drove growth, with management attributing most of the increase to volume and a small part to price, and a surcharge introduced to offset input cost pressure. The call was dominated by questions on losses at the Italian subsidiary V-Shapes (CP Italy), which management attributed almost entirely to the packaging business, and on the rationale for new IP and track-and-trace investments. Management said V-Shapes losses should fall in FY27 and could approach breakeven, though no firm timeline was given.

segments.commentary: Management says the conventional business is at breakeven or slightly profitable; no figures disclosed. Two pilots with top 5-10 Indian pharma companies are nearing completion, with a possible scale-up if results succeed.

segments.commentary: Management cited good traction in core packing, with a pipeline for laminates, food packing and new machines. A new UNNATI packaging-material plant is planned at Guwahati to lower material costs.

segments.commentary: Management says these are at breakeven or better, with 15-20% growth expected for each; CODEOLOGY is being restructured to a smaller core business, and MARKPRINT has contracts in hand. No subsidiary-level sales or profit figures were disclosed.

CP Italy batch of 10 machines being finalized; first two machines had quality and specification issues, and the company is supplying stock machines from India to customers in the interim.
