Management said the Indian coding and marking market is about INR2,000-2,200 crores, growing about 10% a year, and that packaging-sector (pharma, F&B, FMCG) demand is stable while industrial demand fluctuates more.
Gulf and Middle East customers of V-Shapes stopped buying as shipments to the Strait of Hormuz area were blocked.

Management said the Track and Trace market is about INR500-600 crores, and that pharma serialization (top 300 drugs, possibly extended to 946) is a driver, though there is no notification yet on the extension.

qa_highlights.question: Keshav Garg: Are the international acquisition losses a repeat of past vanity acquisitions, and what are the cumulative loss and capital invested?
qa_highlights.answer: Shiva Kabra said the losses are almost entirely in the overseas packaging business (CP Italy) and that the programme has milestones; the investment cycle is longer than expected because the machines needed more stabilisation. He said the IP is now held by Control Print rather than CP Italy and could be licensed. No cumulative loss or investment figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Madhur Rathi: What drove the rise in standalone employee benefit expense from about INR21 crores to INR27-28 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Jaideep Barve said the new wage code (effective November 2025) required a recast of leave-encashment and gratuity liabilities, about INR3.5 crores in impact. Provisions were also made for sales incentives and key management loyalty bonuses.

qa_highlights.question: Vinit Thakur: When will V-Shapes break even, and will losses stop after FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Kabra said V-Shapes losses were about EUR2-2.5 million in FY25 and were guided to about EUR1.5 million this year; breakeven could come this year. He said little further funding is needed after current inventory ships, though some loans to V-Shapes will be recovered.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor: What are the nature of the losses and the course correction for V-Shapes?
qa_highlights.answer: Kabra said about half of V-Shapes costs are R&D, and the rest is contract packaging plus manufacturing and sales. Fixed operating costs were estimated at about USD2-2.5 million per year, with total costs of about EUR2-3 million. Three to four non-productive staff have been let go; investment is going into sales.

qa_highlights.question: Saloni Arya: When do losses subside, what is the Track and Trace market size and margin, and what is the V-Shapes investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Kabra said the Track and Trace market is about INR500-600 crores; pilots are with two large pharma companies. He said margins are at least similar to the coding and marking gross margin, with no numerical margin disclosed. No cumulative V-Shapes investment was given.

qa_highlights.question: Samarth Singh: Where are the quality issues at CP Italy, and what is the total cost base?
qa_highlights.answer: Kabra said the first machines needed multiple engineering visits and the second was swapped for stock, so the company is aiming for 10 identical machines. Jaideep Barve said the CP Italy total cost is about EUR750,000 a year in direct wages, and Kabra said total fixed operating cost is about USD2-2.5 million.

qa_highlights.question: Nikunj Bhanushali: What were the FY26 sales and P&L of CODEOLOGY, MARKPRINT and CP Italy, and what growth is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not disclose subsidiary sales or profit figures; said the entire consolidated overseas loss is CP Italy. Kabra guided CODEOLOGY and MARKPRINT to 15-20% growth and said CODEOLOGY will be scaled down for margin. FY26 printer sales were about 3,064.

522295|2026-06.headline: Control Print standalone operating revenue rose about 5% to ₹105 crore in Q1 FY27, with V-Shapes packaging still loss-making and breakeven pushed to H1 FY28.
522295|2026-06.overview: Standalone total revenue was about ₹107 crore and operating revenue about ₹105 crore versus ₹100 crore a year earlier, with Coding & Marking about 95% of operating revenue. Management attributed the slow quarter to extrusion and pipes demand softness, polymer price volatility linked to the Iran conflict, and a slower consumables pull-through. Consolidated operating revenue was about ₹115 crore against ₹111 crore, with COGS at about 43% versus 42%. The packaging subsidiary (V-Shapes/CP Italy) remains a drag: management now expects the Packaging business to break even only in H1 FY28, and disclosed no new subsidiary cash infusion beyond a planned IP transfer purchase.

Gross margin target of about 60% and EBIT margin of about 30% cited for the core business.

523261|2026-03.headline: Venky's Q4 FY26 margins jumped on broiler realisation; poultry EBIT margin ~14% and Animal Health ~29%, but April–May broiler and chick prices softened.
523261|2026-03.overview: Management said Q4 FY26 improved substantially, driven by better realisation on day-old chicks and broilers, with poultry margins near 14% and Animal Health EBIT margin around 29%. Oil Seed capacity utilisation rose to 65–70%, with a target of about 80% this year and a push to lift outside-group sales to roughly 60–65% of revenue. Management flagged that broiler realisation and chick prices fell from 10–11 May, and maize and soya prices are expected to stay volatile. Full-year FY26 volumes were mixed: commercial broiler birds fell to 8.69 crore from 9.17 crore, while layer chicks rose to 4.57 crore from 4.38 crore.

523301|2026-03.headline: TCPL Packaging Q4 FY26 consolidated income rose over 9% YoY to INR 465 crore, with EBITDA margin at 17.4% including forex-led other income.
523301|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated total income was INR 465 crore (over 9% YoY) and EBITDA including other income was INR 81 crore (17.4% margin), helped by operational export forex gains. FY26 revenue was about INR 1,836 crore (+3% YoY) with EBITDA of INR 318 crore (17.3%). Exports were hit in Q4 by Middle East disruptions, while domestic volumes grew ahead of consumer market trends. Management said margins were pressured by raw material inflation and a lag in passing on price hikes, and the company declined to give margin or export guidance beyond the near term. Finance cost rose on a INR 18 crore mark-to-market loss on ECB, and deferred tax was higher due to capex-related timing differences.

segments.name: Flexible packaging
segments.commentary: Management called FY26 a strong year with healthy utilisation; the last commercialised line runs at optimum level. A fourth line at the unit is expected to be commercialised by year-end FY27, with management expecting its return on assets to beat lines 2 and 3.

segments.name: Folding cartons (consumer products, mainly FMCG and F&B)
segments.commentary: Management said this is more than half of the business. Carton utilisation is lower, with some double-digit scope for growth in existing capacity.

segments.name: Paperboard (Chennai greenfield)
segments.commentary: Utilisation is above 50% and rising on new customer approvals; management expects a good ramp-up ahead.

segments.name: Creative (Noida)
segments.commentary: Management said it just squeaked through to EBITDA break-even in FY25 and improved further in FY26, with a target of cash and net profit in FY27. Electronics demand weakness is a headwind.

segments.name: Recyclable films
segments.commentary: Domestic uptake is weak because EPR rules mandate recycled content, not recyclable packaging. Output is rising through export jobs, and machinery issues are resolved.

guidance_outlook: No formal margin guidance; management expects margins to hold if raw material cost increases stop, and said a prolonged crisis would make further price pass-through difficult.

FY27 capex is guided at about INR 100 crore, similar to last year, with the bulk in flexible packaging and some building expansion; management said the plan is calibrated and could rise if demand picks up.
Exports expected to recover in FY27 if Middle East conditions normalise; management is optimistic about the UK, US, other North America, Europe, Africa and Southeast Asia.
Domestic demand expected to be good for the year, but fuel price and rupee-driven inflation could hit consumer demand in coming quarters.
Utilisation at the Chennai and cylinder facilities is expected to improve over the next one to two quarters.

Electronics volumes are falling due to chip price increases; diversification into other packaging areas is offsetting this.

qa_highlights.answer: Management is fairly optimistic on export recovery if the Middle East normalises, citing scaling in the UK, US, other North America, Europe, Africa and Southeast Asia. It gave no quantified target.

qa_highlights.question: Why is finance cost high despite debt levels, and is the ECB unhedged?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said an INR 18 crore mark-to-market loss on the ECB raised interest cost. It is a notional, non-cash accounting item. Absolute debt grew on a standalone basis and fell marginally on a consolidated basis.

qa_highlights.question: Why is deferred tax so high this year and is it linked to capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the actual tax outgo is already reflected, and the higher deferred tax is a timing difference from capex-driven tax vs accounting depreciation. It said the annual tax rate is in line.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company give a domestic/export revenue split annually?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will consider providing the split, possibly offline, but did not commit.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any pickup in recyclable film demand, and how is Creative progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic recyclable film demand is weak until the government mandates recyclable packaging. Creative reached EBITDA break-even in FY25, improved in FY26, and management aims for cash and net profit in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 capex and is there a plan to expand into new sectors?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is about INR 100 crore, similar to last year, and calibrated given uncertainty. Management said it adds one or two customers almost every month across sectors and is not sector-specific.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY28 margins be higher with Chennai and cylinder ramp-ups?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give guidance, citing geopolitical uncertainty. It said margins should improve with better utilisation if conditions are better.

qa_highlights.question: Is paper cost still rising, and what is the impact of the minimum import price on board?
qa_highlights.answer: Paper cost pressure continues, with virgin board up sharply and recycled board rising steadily. The MIP on board imports gives domestic mills some room, and management expects some price increase is inevitable.

523301|2026-06.headline: TCPL Packaging Q1 FY27 PAT rose ~79% YoY to INR 40 crore on 16% total income growth, and the company announced a INR 125 crore lithium-ion battery separator film venture.
523301|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income rose 16% YoY to INR 495 crore, EBITDA grew 17% to INR 88 crore, and EBITDA margin improved to 18%. Cash profit rose 56% to INR 76 crore and PAT rose nearly 79% to INR 40 crore, helped partly by a normalised interest cost versus a forex/mark-to-market hit in the prior-year quarter. Growth was domestic-led (good double-digit domestic growth, export growth positive but lower) with volumes up high single digits. Management announced a proposed subsidiary to enter lithium-ion battery separator films (INR 125 crore over 18 months, commercial production targeted Q4 FY28) and a ~30% expansion of flexible packaging capacity (INR 50-60 crore).

domestic growth at good double-digit clip

523329|2026-03.headline: FY26 bookings rose 120% to INR 744 crores on Solano Gardens launch, while Q4 margins were hit by about INR 14 crores of one-off expenses.
523329|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 bookings of INR 744 crores (up 120% YoY) and collections of INR 352.1 crores (up ~39%), driven by the Solano Gardens launch where 343 of 433 units sold for over INR 384 crores. Q4 FY26 booking value was INR 382.7 crores and collections INR 96.5 crores. Q4 profitability was dented by about INR 14 crores of one-time items (GST input write-off of ~INR 11 crores plus earlier-project costs). The company added ~INR 2,000 crores GDV through three Lucknow land parcels, two via LDA auctions, and guided to ~INR 4,000 crores total GDV across ongoing, unsold and yet-to-launch projects over 5 to 7 years.

523367|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 net revenue rose 11% YoY to INR3,193 crore, but PBDIT fell to INR400 crore from INR426 crore on sugar cost pressure.
523367|2026-03.overview: DCM Shriram's Q4 FY26 net revenue (net of excise) grew 11% YoY to INR3,193 crore, while PBDIT declined to INR400 crore from INR426 crore. Chemicals revenue rose 32% and Vinyl PBDIT jumped 68%, but Sugar and ethanol PBDIT fell 18% on higher cane prices and Fenesta's margin was diluted by costs. FY26 revenue rose 12% to INR13,538 crore and PBDIT rose 15% to INR1,694 crore, with net debt at INR1,767 crore and ROCE at 13%. Management flagged high PVC price volatility and an unresolved ethanol allocation problem as the main near-term concerns.

qa_highlights.question: Pujan Shah (Molecule Ventures): outlook for PVC pricing given China property weakness and possible closures of inefficient Chinese PVC plants?
qa_highlights.answer: Ajay Shriram said pricing is very volatile and hard to forecast; hoped the rupee depreciation supports import parity and that the 11% import duty returns from 1 July 2026. Current PVC prices around INR81-82/kg; China capacity is so large that closures cannot be verified.

qa_highlights.question: Rohit Nagraj (360 ONE): when will MIP be in place and is there accelerated Chinese dumping or domestic inventory build-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said MIP is under dialogue with government, which has recommended a price considered too low; industry is pressing for a realistic MIP. China was ~50% of India's PVC imports last year, and no timeline can be committed.

qa_highlights.question: Rohit Nagraj: how will Middle East alumina capacity outages affect the global caustic balance and domestic pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Aditya Shriram said regional balances matter and the impact of one demand region cannot be directly correlated to price; expects robust Indian demand long term with some short-term volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Ahmed Madha (Unifi Capital): ECH utilisation and margin outlook, and epoxy break-even timing?
qa_highlights.answer: ECH running at 60-70% utilisation, ramp-up over one to two quarters; management expects healthy ECH margins if raw material and product prices hold. Epoxy/advanced materials expected to reach break-even in FY27, with Amit Agarwal saying slightly better than break-even this year.

qa_highlights.question: Ahmed Madha: is ECH margin still in the 20-25% range and will chemicals EBITDA margin (about 20% in FY26) improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Agarwal said Bharuch should be assessed as an integrated complex; complex revenue +38% and EBITDA +50% last year; new products rose from ~14% to ~34-35% of revenue. Aditya Shriram declined to give a margin number.

qa_highlights.question: Ahmed Madha: will sugar margins be material in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Agarwal said margins are lower than last year, but record-low industry inventory (~4 million tonnes) should lift prices; shrinkage expected but not significant. The export ban has only short-term sentiment impact.

qa_highlights.question: Riya Mehta (Aequitas): Fenesta cost pass-through, margins and demand after aluminium price rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Agarwal said retail customers are hard to pass cost to, while institutional contracts pass through costs beyond a tolerance level; margin is hit until then. Demand is good with a record order book.

523367|2026-06.headline: DCM Shriram Q1 FY27 net revenue rose 9% to INR3,564 crore and PBDIT 12% to INR364 crore; reported PAT of INR693 crore includes INR474 crore one-time tax credit.

Vinyl PBDIT nearly doubled on price gains despite a 25% fall in PVC volumes, while Bioseed swung to a loss on delayed monsoon. Reported PAT of INR693 crore includes a INR474 crore one-time tax adjustment and INR79 crore of other one-time gains; underlying PAT was INR147 crore, up 28%. Management flagged weak rural demand, soft Q2 vinyl offtake and a 15-20% Kharif sowing shortfall as near-term headwinds.

qa_highlights.question: Caustic soda price outlook for the near term and FY27, and current chlorine price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it normally avoids forward price statements, but noted ECU is just below INR30,000/t and expects that level or higher. Chlorine is at minus INR7,000 to minus INR8,000/t.

qa_highlights.question: Why is SFS profitability up on flat top line, and how will Kharif profitability shape up if monsoon holds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited farmer reach, new R&D products and market credibility. It said monsoon has been good only in pockets, sowing is 15-20% lower, and it cannot project Aug-Sep outcomes.

qa_highlights.question: Will more capacity be diverted to grain ethanol given better sugar prices, and how is ethanol profitability set to move?
qa_highlights.answer: Grain-based ethanol can run up to 260 KLD and will be optimised for margins, which are currently good on maize. Management said it does not plan to add capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the INR400-odd crore tax reversal and the cash tax impact going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: It relates to a six-year ITAT-backed position, with MAT credit of INR376 crore. P&L tax stays at 25%, but cash tax outgo is about 19% for at least five years.

qa_highlights.question: Crushing outlook for next season and sugar price expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Too early to call next year's cane harvest given the monsoon. Sugar prices, around INR40-50/kg per the analyst, are expected to stay firm for the next couple of months.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for urea margins given global price spikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Urea pricing is governed by FICC rules, so international prices do not hit domestic makers. Government is paying on time; gas price spikes are a pass-through that can strain cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Why did debt rise and what is the year-end net borrowing outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt did not rise in Q1; the comparison is year-on-year, covering about INR450 crore of acquisitions and about INR1,000 crore of capex. Year-end net borrowing should be similar, with about INR200 crore reduction possible; debt/EBITDA is kept below 1.5x, with AA+ rating.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the group demerger and expected Bioseed recovery in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is committed to the demerger and aims to file the application with government in FY27, with no firm timeline. Bioseed: large part of Kharif volume is lost and no firm recovery was guided for Q2.

523367|2026-09.headline: DCM Shriram Q2 FY27 net revenue rose 22% YoY to Rs 3,977 crore, but PBDIT fell to Rs 319 crore from Rs 408 crore on chemicals input costs.

Management declared a 200% interim dividend (Rs 62.38 crore) and flagged a demerger targeted for Q1 FY28 board consideration.

523642|2026-03.headline: PI Industries FY26 revenue ₹67,137 mn with ~25% EBITDA margin; Q4 revenue ₹15,652 mn up sequentially, FY27 guided to growth led by H2 exports recovery.
523642|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was ₹15,652 mn, up sequentially as guided last quarter, and FY26 consolidated revenue was ₹67,137 mn with a stated 25% EBITDA margin and ₹34,265 mn cash. AgChem exports declined on lower volumes amid a global downcycle, while domestic demand was hit by channel inventory, price pressure, and lower acreages. Management guided to revenue growth in FY27, with exports recovering in H2, but declined to give a specific growth number or margin guidance beyond maintaining last year's average gross margin. Pharma grew 40% for the year and biologicals are targeted to scale, with the first homegrown NCE (Pioxaniliprole) nearing market.

523642|2026-06.headline: PI Industries Q1 FY27 revenue Rs 17,023 million with 57% gross margin and 22% EBITDA margin; FY27 growth guided to lower single digit.

Exports saw volume down 8% and value down 12% YoY, while domestic volume grew 12% but revenue only 3%. Subsidiary losses, driven by global biologicals and pharma ramp-up, were about Rs 100 crore at EBITDA level in the quarter. Management reiterated FY27 revenue growth in the lower single digits and expects FY27 to beat FY26 on an export recovery in the second half.

523694|2026-06.headline: Apcotex Q1 FY27 revenue hit record Rs 526 crore (+40% YoY) and PAT rose 311% to Rs 79 crore, helped by price realisations and inventory gains.
523694|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue of Rs 526 crore, up 40% YoY, with operating EBITDA of Rs 117 crore (22.3% margin vs 10.3%) and PAT of Rs 79 crore (15.01% margin vs 5.11%). Volumes fell 10-12% because exports to the MENA region were hit by West Asia disruption, freight costs and logistics issues, while domestic volumes rose about 10%. Management said inventory gains added roughly 2% to EBITDA margin. Working capital rose on higher raw material prices, and net cash fell to about Rs 40 crore from about Rs 70 crore at March 2026 (Q&A noted a figure of about Rs 30 crore).

segments.name: Nitrile latex (NBR/XNBR)
segments.commentary: Margins improved in Q1 versus prior years; management said they were above 15% in Q1 but did not reach that level through FY25-26. NBR is capacity-constrained with ~30% Indian market share, the rest met by imports.

segments.name: Synthetic latex / other products
segments.commentary: Management said margins expanded across all segments in Q1, not just nitrile latex. Company cites about 25 new products added and eight end-industries served.

segments.name: Apco build (small segment)
segments.commentary: Described as growing but still a small part of the business; no numbers given.

guidance_outlook: Average EBITDA margin guidance remains 15-16%; management declined to call Q1 margins sustainable and said it expects some quarters lower and some higher.
NBR capacity expansion expected on stream by Q1 FY28 (possibly April 2028); SB latex and other synthetic latex capex about a couple of months later (around June 2028).

Combined capex of about Rs 220 crore (Rs 130-140 crore for NBR debottlenecking/expansion adding roughly 100% of NBR capacity, rest for synthetic latex). Management expects about Rs 600 crore additional top line, roughly 40% uplift from announced projects.
Decision on a third (stage two) nitrile latex expansion expected in 3-4 months, after watching margins and Asian/Malaysian capacity.
Management expects volumes to rebound quickly once the West Asia conflict eases; said volumes in MENA may not grow near term while oil prices stay high.
capex_capacity: Capex of about Rs 220 crore is in progress; only 15-20% spent so far, mainly advances and civil work. Major equipment deliveries are due in Q3 and Q4 FY27.

Plants run on dual fuel (gas and coal), and each raw material has multiple sources.
Capex so far is self-funded; management expects to take debt in the next couple of quarters.
demand_pricing: Volumes fell 10-12% YoY and QoQ, entirely due to exports; MENA customers were hit by Strait of Hormuz disruption. Domestic volumes rose about 10%.

Domestic demand described as strong across paper, construction, rubber goods and others. Ocean freight costs were absorbed by the company on exports.

Competition: no anti-dumping duty in India currently. Management said Europe and the US have no NBR expansion announced; some Asian expansions are coming but expected to be absorbed in three to five years.
Working capital rose because of higher raw material values. Inventory days were unchanged; the increase came from price, not quantity.

qa_highlights.question: What made the business resilient this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited deliberate investments in dual fuel, multiple raw material sources, quick procurement and inventory planning. It said these had been built over several years.

qa_highlights.question: Can throughput double in five years?
qa_highlights.answer: Announced projects should add about Rs 600 crore to top line, roughly 40%. Further doubling depends on market support, and management sees no reason it cannot happen.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the NBR expansion approved now?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex fell to Rs 130-140 crore for almost 100% NBR capacity via debottlenecking, from Rs 200-250 crore earlier. Margins had improved and there is no major NBR expansion globally, so returns were justified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net cash position and capex spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Net cash of about Rs 40 crore, down from about Rs 70 crore at March, partly due to higher working capital. Only 15-20% of the Rs 220 crore capex has been spent.

qa_highlights.question: Is demand or realisation rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisations were higher on average in Q1 but are now falling with oil. Domestic demand is strong across sectors; exports are the main issue, mainly MENA.

523694|2026-09.headline: Apcotex Q2 FY27 revenue rose 48% YoY to Rs 499 crore, but EBITDA margin eased to 11.69% as gross margins compressed.
523694|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 operating revenue was Rs 499 crore (+48% YoY) on 7% volume growth, with operating EBITDA of Rs 58 crore (+44% YoY) and PAT of Rs 35 crore (+38% YoY). EBITDA margin was 11.69% versus 12.06% a year earlier, and PAT margin was 6.98%. H1 FY27 was the company's strongest half-year, with revenue of Rs 1,025 crore (+44%), EBITDA of Rs 175 crore (+121%, margin 17.12%) and PAT of Rs 114 crore (+156%). Management attributed the Q2 margin dip to high raw material prices, about 1.5% inventory losses, and more aggressive pricing to win export volumes.

segments.commentary: Sole Indian producer, entirely import-dependent; plant has run at full capacity for about 1.5 to 2 years. Capex project targeted for commissioning around April 2027. H1 NBR margin said to be slightly higher than synthetic latex.

segments.name: Synthetic latex (SBR)
segments.commentary: Serves about five industries; construction strongest, paper and textiles decent, tyres okay, carpets a laggard due to MENA dependence. SBR latex plant at Valia expected around Q2 of next year.

Competitor shutdowns in Q1 benefited the company, which kept plants running; overcapacity in nitrile latex persists from COVID-era additions.
Carpet volumes hit by US tariffs, the war and high ocean freight; management said Q2 carpet volumes were broadly flat YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why are gross margins at a four-quarter low, and what drove the rise in export volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited high raw material prices, about 1.5% inventory losses in the quarter, and more aggressive pricing. Exports improved with better ship availability to Saudi Arabia and Fujairah, plus orders from other markets. EBITDA per ton and ROCE were better YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the nitrile latex cycle and does oversupply persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Running close to full capacity; Q2 margins normalised from a strong Q1 but are much better than the last three years. Overcapacity from COVID-era additions remains even after some smaller and older plants shut. Expansion decision deferred for a couple more quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a timeline and funding breakup for the Rs 210 crore expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: NBR commissioning targeted for about April 2027, with two to three years to full utilisation. Management said about Rs 65 crore is spent and Rs 155 crore remains, but did not give a debt versus internal accrual split in the answer.

qa_highlights.question: Which synthetic latex industries are growing or lagging?
qa_highlights.answer: Construction (repairs, waterproofing, oil drilling) has grown strongly; paper and textiles are decent and tyres okay. Carpets are the laggard due to MENA and Western market exposure from tariffs, war and freight costs.

qa_highlights.question: What long-term volume growth is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 10% average volume CAGR over three to five years, driven by population and GDP growth in India and Southeast Asia, plus substitution of European supply in MENA.

qa_highlights.question: Is the sequential Q2-to-Q3 decline a pattern, and is there a strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged the Q1-to-Q2 seasonal decline from monsoon-linked demand. It said it had not analysed Q2-to-Q3 patterns and would review five years of data. It urged investors to focus on annual trends, given oil-linked inventory gains and losses.

523704|2026-09.headline: Mastek Q2 FY27 revenue rose 2.4% QoQ cc to $107.3M, but 12-month backlog fell 7.7% QoQ to $286.2M and EBITDA margin slipped to 14.4%.

Operating EBITDA margin fell about 100 bps QoQ to 14.4%, mainly from increments and ESOPs (190 bps), partly offset by AI-led efficiency and extra working days. The 12-month backlog fell 7.7% QoQ to $286.2M, attributed to a delayed US federal start and slower UK consumption, though it grew 2.3% YoY in USD. Management reiterated that FY27 should beat FY26, with North America turning around from H2 and UK Healthcare recovering after recontracting.

segments.name: Senior Living
segments.commentary: FY26 bookings Rs 570 crore (+55% YoY); management targets over Rs 700 crore in FY27. Five projects with GDV over Rs 6,500 crore to launch in 12-24 months across Chennai, Bangalore and Bombay-Pune.

segments.name: Residential (Gurugram, Jaipur, Bhiwadi, Pune, Chennai, Jamshedpur)
segments.commentary: Q4 bookings driven by Gurugram Aaroham Phase-I/II (about Rs 833 crore at launch). Jaipur and Jamshedpur realisations now above Rs 7,000 per sq ft; management flagged early oversupply signs in Gurugram and Pune.

guidance_outlook: FY27 pre-sales target of Rs 2,200 crore, with Senior Living target above Rs 700 crore.

Launches planned in FY27: Ashiana Oma (Jaipur, about 10 acres, Rs 7,500-8,000 per sq ft, within a couple of months), Ashiana Aaranya and Tattvam (Q4 FY27), Aaroham Phase-III, and at least one phase in each Senior Living project.
Margin outlook: FY27 full-year margin to be better than FY26 and FY28 better than FY27, with quarterly volatility; Malhar Phase-II and Anmol Phase-III are low-margin.
Reported ROE of above 20% targeted for FY27; FY30 cumulative PAT guidance of Rs 2,000 crore reiterated as on track.
Blended realisation expected to move in a Rs 9,000-11,000 per sq ft range, with about Rs 10,000 as a near-term aim.
Construction cost inflation expected at 8-10% YoY in FY27; no inflation underwritten at land acquisition.
Capital to be redeployed into growth rather than buybacks or large dividends; Senior Living to receive the bulk of capital.
Senior Living projects targeted at 30-35% project-level margins (35-40% gross, 5-6% selling cost).
capex_capacity: Land bank of about 96 lakh sq ft post recent additions (about 4x annual throughput); management says more land must be added this year.

Acquired 8.83 acres in Raigad for about Rs 450 crore sales potential; Panvel (agreement, about Rs 1,000 crore); Vadgaon (28.5 acres, about 20 lakh sq ft, Rs 1,800-2,000 crore GDV); Bangalore (about 11 lakh sq ft, CP resolution pending, about 2 months).
Phases totalling about 25 lakh sq ft to be launched by FY31 across Vatsalya, Advik, Swarang and Aaroham.
Delivery timing: Oma phase by FY30; Aaranya and Tattvam partly FY31; Wavarle, Vadgaon and Bangalore launched in FY28 with FY30-31 deliveries.
Mahindra World City Jaipur lease terminated after 18 months without approvals; Aaranya (22.7 acres, Chennai) is a separate, ongoing project.
demand_pricing: Gurugram: signs of oversupply, with unsold inventory up for two consecutive quarters after heavy launches; management says sustained trend for about four more quarters would cause oversupply.
Pune: early oversupply signs; Bhiwadi, Jamshedpur and Jaipur show no oversupply yet.
Senior Living sales are mostly direct (about 40% Bombay, 40% Pune and 20% rest of India/NRI at Amodh); channel partner use is limited.
Amodh newer phases at about Rs 8,200-8,300 per sq ft; Amodh Phase-III around Rs 8,500 per sq ft used as the Vadgaon benchmark.
Competition in Senior Living seen as market-expanding; few peers building large (12-15 acre) projects with comparable amenities.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Mahindra World City (Jaipur) lease terminated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the counterparty could not obtain social infrastructure approvals after about 18 months, so the transaction could not proceed; the lease was terminated, with scope to restart later.

qa_highlights.question: Project-level margin and cost breakup for Senior Living?
qa_highlights.answer: Project margins are expected at 30-35%; gross margin 35-40%, selling cost 5-6%. Land is 10-20% and hard construction 40-50% of revenue, with soft costs about 5%.

qa_highlights.question: Construction cost inflation assumption?
qa_highlights.answer: No inflation underwritten at land purchase; management expects 8-10% construction cost increase in FY27 YoY on current information.

qa_highlights.question: Is annuity or leasing a major Senior Living revenue stream?
qa_highlights.answer: Not within five years; yields are low and leasing deposit structures are not viable. Home sales remain the main profit source, and assisted living is outsourced partly to Epoch Elder Care (Nirmay, Bhiwadi).

qa_highlights.question: Is there oversupply in the markets?
qa_highlights.answer: No oversupply yet overall. Gurugram and Pune show early signs; Jaipur, Jamshedpur and Bhiwadi show none.

qa_highlights.question: What is the class action suit status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company has moved the Delhi High Court against class action applicability; a ruling is hoped for within FY27, but consumer complaints will continue for the filers regardless.

risks_watch: Construction cost inflation (8-10% expected in FY27) and labour and material shortages affecting delivery timelines.
Low-margin projects Malhar Phase-II and Anmol Phase-III may dent quarterly margins; FY27 ROE above 20% has little room for slippage.
Oversupply signs in Gurugram and Pune, which carry large inventory.
Class action litigation over an older Kolkata/Pune-area project (Project Maitri-related disputes settled separately); outcome timing uncertain.
Execution of Bangalore land (CP still pending) and Panvel pricing not yet fixed; Maharashtra senior living policy not yet notified.
Management flagged that a sustained rise in unsold inventory in Gurugram would signal oversupply.
523716|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on Senior Living growth and FY30 targets, but guarded on macro and geopolitical impact, and evasive on project-level pricing and investment detail. Cautious on Gurugram and Pune supply, and openly defensive on the class action suit.
key_quotes: We are in the bottom of the top tier of brands in Gurugram. We want to get into a higher tier there for the product we are in.
The profitability in the next five years will continue to come from home sales.
I think we are expecting about 8-10% increase in construction costs in this financial year, on a year-on-year basis, as of now.
There is no oversupply yet. Signs of some oversupply in Gurugram and Pune are visible.

523716|2026-06.headline: Ashiana Housing Q1 FY27 revenue fell to INR107 crores from INR293 crores as handovers slipped; management reiterates INR2,200 crores FY27 presales target.
523716|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 bookings were INR358 crores across 234 units (3.6 lakh sq ft), down from the strong prior quarter, while collections rose 6% YoY to INR409 crores. Average realisation rose 37% YoY to INR9,923 per sq ft on product mix. Reported revenue was INR107 crores, driven by Phase 1 handover at Ashiana Nitara, Jaipur; management attributed the shortfall to handover timing, with OC for Anmol Phase 3 and Amarah Phase 1 (about INR532 crores of revenue) arriving mid-July and shifting into Q2. The company bought 28.55 acres at Vadgaon, Maval, Pune, its largest Senior Living land deal (about 20 lakh sq ft, potential sales value around INR1,800 crores).

Presales were about INR570 crores last year; management targets about INR1,500 crores by FY29-30 and about 25% CAGR long term. Five projects are deployed, and the company aims for about INR10,000 crores GDV in Senior Living.

segments.commentary: Management flagged a near-term lack of inventory to sell in these key markets, which is expected to dampen presales in the next year or two. Ashiana Aaroham Phase 3 (Gurugram) is the big H2 launch.

segments.commentary: Ongoing portfolio mix at 36%, per the analyst's figure. Management said the mix shift is toward Senior Living, not a pivot to premium homes.

qa_highlights.question: What drives H2 bookings and confidence in FY27 guidance after a soft Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said July 2026 sales beat all of Q1; cumulative FY27 sales were about INR859 crores by 31 July. The big H2 launch is Aaroham Phase 3 (Gurugram) in Q3 or Q4, and H1 is expected to exit at INR1,050-1,100 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainable presales trajectory over 3-5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a dip in presales for a year or two due to thin inventory in Gurugram, Jaipur and Bhiwadi, with recovery in FY28-29 or FY29-30. Capital is shifting to Senior Living, with a target of about INR1,500 crores of Senior Living presales by FY29-30.

qa_highlights.question: Why ROE expectations changed from 20%+ to 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 15% has been the long-term goal and was reached on a reported basis last year. It expects about 20% in FY27 and says 15% should be the floor. The margin framework is about 30% gross, 12% SG&A, 18% PBT and 12-13% PAT margin, which should give teens ROE and about 20% with further improvement.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 revenue so low, and is it a steady-state run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was not normal. Anmol Phase 3 and Amarah Phase 1 OCs came in mid-July, so about INR532 crores of revenue shifts into Q2. Management asked investors to judge on a year-on-year basis and pointed to the FY27 revenue indication of about INR2,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Units sold fell from 407 to 234 YoY. Deliberate or volume slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was not entirely deliberate, citing lower inventory in some markets. It pointed to the July launch and reiterated the INR2,200 crores presales target.

qa_highlights.question: Vadgaon payback and underwriting?
qa_highlights.answer: Underwriting assumes INR9,000-10,000 per sq ft on 20 lakh sq ft, or INR1,800-2,000 crores of revenue. Sales are planned at about 2 lakh sq ft per year, with a launch in about 18 months. The NCD was issued by the landowners, who keep a 25% stake plus a 6% revenue share.

qa_highlights.question: Capex for the deals in pipeline and IFC partnership status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the FY27 deployment budget is about INR800 crores, including Q1 deals and deals in active discussion. The IFC platform is exhausted or lapsed because of ticket-size caps. There is no active agreement, though discussions on future capital are ongoing.

523754|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 14.8% to INR315.8 crores and PBT to INR16.99 crores, but Q4 PBT fell to INR6.4 crores on a March raw-material spike.
523754|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 revenue of INR315.8 crores (up 14.8% from INR275.1 crores) and PBT of INR16.99 crores versus INR10.7 crores in FY25, despite a INR2.1 crore past-service personnel cost. Q4 revenue grew about 11%, but Q4 PBT fell to INR6.4 crores from INR9.4 crores as PE pipe prices jumped roughly 58-59% in February 2026 and stayed high in March. Receivables built up sharply in a few key subsidy states, and operating free cash flow has been negative over multi-year periods, which an analyst pressed on. Management pointed to non-subsidy share rising to 35% in FY26 (from 3% in FY20 per the call) and to a projects pipeline of about INR54-55 crores for FY27.

segments.commentary: About 35% of FY26 revenue, an all-time high, spanning projects, ISI-grade farmer sales, institutional sales, thin-wall pipes and mulch sheets. Management expects this share to keep rising, with no timeline given.

segments.name: Irrigation projects (government tenders)
segments.commentary: About a quarter of total business (about INR75 crores per analyst's math, confirmed as a quarter). Opening FY27 order visibility is INR54 crores, with a possible further INR20 crores in coming weeks. Projects drive higher variable/other expenses but lower raw-material cost.

GST cut from 12% to 5% seen as a medium-term demand positive.

qa_highlights.question: How much raw material price increase is expected for FY27, how much can be passed on, and what is the EBITDA margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called raw material volatility an FY27 risk, with mitigation via product mix, geography mix and timing of procurement. It declined to give a margin target and said it would selectively raise prices in non-subsidy markets.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses jump?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly a higher share of projects revenue in Q4, which carries higher variable expenses but lower raw-material cost, plus some cost increases.

qa_highlights.question: Cash flow has been negative over several years; when will the non-subsidy mix invert, and how much of INR217 crore receivables is non-subsidy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 80-90% of receivables are from subsidy business. It expects cash flows to improve as two southern states and one western state resume payments, and cited thin-wall and mulch sheet products with better cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for capex in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is planned annually, mainly for productivity and current product lines, with capacity expansion secondary; management expects quick payback on each spend.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost rise about 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly the new labour code and contractual alignment of employee benefits; not headcount additions or variable pay.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of below-normal monsoon on demand, and timing of government price action?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects any monsoon impact to show mainly in H2 FY27 and is monitoring it. Price relief via the government is a daily discussion with no date; difficult to call.

qa_highlights.question: Project size and FY27 order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Plans to step up project size, not drastically. Opening order visibility is INR54 crores (earlier cited 55), with a possible INR20 crore upside.

523796|2026-03.headline: Viceroy Hotels Q4 FY26 revenue rose 35.3% YoY to INR 49.5 crore, with EBITDA margin up 183 bps to 31.4%, aided by the Marriott Executive Apartments acquisition.

Growth was driven mainly by consolidation of Marriott Executive Apartments (75 rooms, acquired 1 January 2026), which contributed its first quarter. Management said March was softer on geopolitical tensions and the West Asia conflict, with ADR and occupancy moderating at the existing hotels. PAT fell to about INR 6 crore, which management attributed to higher depreciation and finance costs from renovation and acquisition debt, and to a deferred-tax benefit booked in the prior year.

523796|2026-06.headline: Viceroy Hotels Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 77% to INR44.9 crore and EBITDA rose 144% to INR11.8 crore, with PAT turning positive at INR1.4 crore.

523828|2026-03.headline: Menon Bearings FY26 consolidated PAT rose 53.41% to INR 38.25 crore; Q4 PAT up 108.55% YoY, with management guiding 20-22% EBITDA margin.

Management guided to 25% annual volume growth, 20-22% EBITDA margin for the next two years, and INR 500 crore revenue by FY28. Alkop (aluminium) growth was flagged as a key swing factor after a slow prior two years.

523828|2026-06.headline: Menon Bearings Q1 FY27 consolidated sales rose 36.57% to INR91.79 crores and PAT 67.35%, with management reiterating INR360 crore FY27 revenue as conservative.
523828|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly sales, EBITDA, PBT and PAT for Q1 FY27, with consolidated sales of INR91.79 crores (up 36.57%) and PBT of INR18.51 crores (up 67.36%). Standalone bi-metal sales rose to INR67.06 crores (up ~40%). Growth was attributed to export and new customer wins following a June 2026 US and Canada marketing trip, plus a shift in product mix toward brakes, where EBITDA margin reached about 25%. Management said the FY27 revenue guidance of INR360 crores is conservative, and described a domestic RFQ pipeline of over INR75 crores. Several new-business timelines (Alkop US customers, railway brake approval) run into FY28 and beyond.

segments.name: Bi-metal (Menon Bearings)
segments.commentary: Q1 standalone sales INR67.06 crores; EBITDA margin around 21%+ per management. Utilisation about 80% on machinery basis; Rs 9-10 crore capex this year expected to add 25-30% capacity.

segments.name: Aluminium (Menon Alkop)
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin around 21%. Utilisation 65-70%. Management targets Alkop revenue of INR100 crores this year and INR125 crores next year; quarterly run rate cited by an analyst at about INR21 crores.

segments.name: Brakes (Menon Brakes)
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin about 25% in Q1, up from about 12-14% previously, attributed mainly to product mix and lower Dubai/Africa export volumes. Utilisation 65-70%. Railway dynamometer expected by end-August 2026, with testing rig running by September-end.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of INR360 crores, which management called conservative; mid-20% growth possible, with internal target of INR500 crores reached sooner than 2030.
Consolidated EBITDA margin expected to sustain around 20-21% over time; management said brake margin of 25% may fall next quarter.
Additional business of INR65-75 crores for current and next FY, subject to good monsoon and no worsening geopolitics.
Domestic RFQ list above INR75 crores; at 75-80% conversion, management expects more than INR60 crores of additional business within this year and next.
Export share of revenue expected to rise to about 37% next year; FY27 export share was described as around 24-30% historically.
capex_capacity: Bi-metal: Rs 9-10 crores capex this FY to add roughly 25-30% capacity; expected to yield revenue above INR25 crores. Peak bi-metal revenue on current capacity cited above INR400 crores.
Alkop: about INR4 crores capex this year; 65,000 sq ft new building with 25,000-30,000 sq ft still available for machines already ordered.

Brakes: dynamometer under construction, expected by end-August 2026; railway approval, then testing for about one year. Railway business INR5-6 crores in year one, scaling to INR25-30 crores within two years.

Management says current infrastructure supports up to about INR500 crores revenue; about seven acres of empty land at the aluminium plant. New land for bi-metal being evaluated for the next two years.
Future capex asset turn about 2.5x; capex to be funded through internal accruals, no fresh loans for bi-metal and Alkop.
demand_pricing: Alkop: RFQs, NDAs and vendor profiling from Magna, Allison Transmission, Linamar-type US customers after June 2026 US and Canada trip; management cites INR50-60 crores potential, realisation expected in 9-12 months (targeting 6-7 months). Samples by 2027.
Bi-metal engine bearing: began receiving RFQs and orders from US customers; supply expected from Q3-Q4 FY27.

Africa: bearings, bushes, washers estimated at about INR9 crores; brake linings INR6-7 crores; existing Dubai distributor business INR7-8 crores per year. Merchant export orders were stalled for three months due to Strait of Hormuz disruption; new orders require 100% advance for the initial six months.
Aluminium realisation above INR900 per unit now, up from about INR700 when aluminium was about INR250-300/kg; aluminium rates now INR340-370.
Competition: China pressure in Dubai and Africa for brake linings; company keeps minimum margins on these exports.
EV share in Alkop about 4-5% now, targeting about 8% within two years; Tata EV parts moved to a 1,600-ton press.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue expected from brakes in FY27 and railway timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Dynamometer by end-August; RDSO vendor code registered; railway audit then approval; INR5-6 crores in year one, INR25-30 crores within two years. Management declined to give precise OEM numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Africa revenue potential and payment terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Bearings, bushes, washers about INR9 crores; brake linings INR6-7 crores; Dubai distributor INR7-8 crores a year. Aluminium excluded; new merchant exporters require 100% advance for initial six months.

qa_highlights.question: Alkop business visibility and FY28 expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Targets INR100 crores this year and INR125 crores next year. US RFQs and NDAs received; new business takes 9-12 months to realise. Europe visit planned for September.

qa_highlights.question: Bi-metal capacity beyond current utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation about 85-87% by one measure, about 80% by management's machinery-based count. Capex of INR9-10 crores adds 25-30% capacity; third shift available.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 INR360 crore guidance conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called INR360 crores conservative, declined to raise the number, and said Q4 would be better.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainability of margins with raw-material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated margin 20-21% expected over time; brake margin of 25% driven by product mix and may fall next quarter.

risks_watch: Brake margin of 25% is product-mix driven and may fall; management expects consolidated margins of 20-21%.
Monsoon and geopolitical conditions (Strait of Hormuz, war) cited as conditions for the INR65-75 crore additional business.

Raw-material and consumables cost volatility: aluminium up sharply; carbide tools up about 300% per management.
Dependence on export: about 60% of order book is export; US concentration; tariff impact noted earlier.

523828|2026-09.headline: Menon Bearings guides 30%+ growth for FY27 and FY28 after H1 FY27 income from operations of INR 194.9 crore (+47% YoY).
523828|2026-09.overview: Management reported record quarterly sales, EBITDA, PBT and PAT on a consolidated basis for Q2 FY27, with total income up 58.6% YoY, EBITDA up 103.8%, PBT up 123% and PAT up 117%. H1 EBITDA rose 77%, PBT 92% and PAT 89.55%, with cash and bank balances including mutual funds of INR 25.69 crore. Management said it expects over 30% growth in FY27 and FY28, citing additional business of INR 30 crore in FY27, INR 131 crore in FY28 and INR 157 crore in FY29, plus a Europe pipeline of over INR 35 crore. Management attributed margin resilience to productivity gains (stated at 25%), material-usage reductions and automation, while noting raw material inflation (tin up 72%, copper up 50%, steel up 12%).

financial_highlights.metric: Total income growth (consolidated, Q2 FY27 YoY)
H1 FY27 PBT and PAT growth
Cash and bank balance incl. mutual funds
Operating cash flow H1 FY27 (analyst figure, not confirmed by management)
financial_highlights.value: ~INR 20 crore vs INR 23 crore for full FY26

segments.name: Bearings (engine/bimetal)
segments.commentary: Management cited an EBITDA margin of about 23% for the bearing segment. OEM business grew about 50% YoY in Q2 per management.

segments.name: Menon Alkop (aluminium/EV and non-auto)
segments.commentary: Alkop margin stated at 18-19%. Export value and volume growing; EV business growing about 20%; about 54 new parts developed in last two years. Auto is only about 18-20% of Alkop revenue.

segments.name: Brakes
segments.commentary: Brake segment margins stated at 30-35%, depending on product mix; management expects brakes to lead replacement-market growth.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export growth above 75% YoY in Q2 per management; exports at about 34-35% of revenue, about 80% of which goes to the USA.

guidance_outlook: FY27 growth of more than 30% in revenue, with FY28 also expected above 30% if conditions hold.

Additional business estimated at INR 30 crore (FY27), INR 131 crore (FY28) and INR 157 crore (FY29), excluding a Europe opportunity of INR 35 crore to INR 40 crore expected to convert over a longer time.
Management indicated revenue could reach INR 500 crore 'next year or maybe year after', versus INR 300 crore in FY26; H2 expected to be stronger than H1.
EBITDA margin expected to range 20-22% in normal course, with a target of about 23% for next year.
Roughly 20% of the 30%+ growth expected from volume, with the balance from price revisions.
capex_capacity: Automation and robotic cells planned: about INR 5 crore in Alkop and about INR 4.5 crore in Bearings over the next 12-15 months, with ROI stated at 2.5-3.5 years.
Bearing lines: about 16 bimetal lines (from around 90 semi-automatic machines) moving to single-piece flow, expected to save about 3 people per line, roughly 50 employees in bearings.
AI-based automated visual inspection systems: some implemented, others under development; expected in place within 9-12 months. About 10 lakh engine bearing parts inspected monthly.
Capex funded from internal accruals; no term loan availed for more than six months.
Infrastructure stated as in place, with capacity added by adding machines as needed.
demand_pricing: Raw material inflation: tin up 72%, copper up 50%, steel up 12%, with average price increases near 50% YoY per management; pass-through to customers via pre-agreed formula, with a one-quarter lag absorbed.
Aluminium prices fell about 15% from May-June peak, benefiting Alkop, and vendor prices also reduced.
Headcount up about 5% YoY against about 30% revenue growth; sales and distribution costs rose on US/Europe freight.
Replacement market growing strongly, with management citing HCV, LCV and passenger vehicles growing 14-15% and EV around 20% over last six months.
Tractor schedules at all-time high despite drought-like conditions in Maharashtra; management says tractor share has fallen from 54% to 34% of the business over 10 years.
Working capital: US customers hold about 3 months of inventory in their warehouses; air freight used where Strait of Hormuz disruption extends shipping times.

qa_highlights.question: Did the decline in aluminium prices help Alkop margins in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, lower aluminium prices benefit Alkop; vendor pricing was also reduced in the quarter, adding to profit. No quantification given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did sales promotion and other expenses rise (from about INR 4.7 crore to INR 8.15 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher replacement market activity and substantially higher export freight to the USA and Europe, which raised sales and distribution costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin expand despite a 7-percentage-point gross margin decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lower raw material consumption through process improvements, 25% productivity gains and better overhead absorption; price revisions to customers are a routine pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: Is EV share of Alkop on track for 8-10% in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management said it will be at or above that range, but the EV share of total will stay roughly flat as domestic and other exports also grow.

qa_highlights.question: What are the EBITDA margin expectations and targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin will range 20-22% and it targets about 23% next year; competitors cited at 7-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Where does the company stand in the auto cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tractor schedules are rising despite drought in Maharashtra, HCV/LCV/PV growing 14-15%, and EV growing 20%; de-risking through non-auto applications is ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: Is the working capital and inventory improvement sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory build for US customers (about 3 months stock) is complete; future inventory will rise modestly with volumes, and borrowing costs have stayed flat despite turnover growth.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation (tin, copper, steel) and the one-quarter lag before price pass-through may compress margins.
Concentration in USA exports (about 80% of exports) and trade policy volatility; Europe pipeline (INR 35-40 crore) not yet converted and expected to take 9-12 months from RFQ to sales.
Shipping disruptions (Strait of Hormuz) increasing working capital and air freight costs.
Management's FY27 and FY28 growth targets rely on the stated INR 30 crore/131 crore additional business pipeline; delivery against these will be the key check.
Tractor exposure (about 34% of engine bearing business per management) amid drought in Maharashtra.
Other income and intercompany eliminations mean Q1 and Q2 figures do not sum to H1; standalone and consolidated figures differ.
523828|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and promotional, with strong emphasis on record results and forward growth. Management was specific on historical numbers and margins but gave looser, qualitative answers on five-year aspirations, Europe timing and the origin of the margin gains, and repeatedly qualified targets as forward-looking.
key_quotes: There will be more than 30% growth for this year, FY27, and similarly in '27-'28 also we expect, if all the things are in place, it will be more than 30% again
So we are not looking at top line to increase significantly. We want our EBITDA margins, our PAT margins to grow at what numbers we have now.
So in the next 9 to 12 months, a lot of automation and visual systems are getting in place where we save on manpower, we save on time that leads in productivity, and quality is more focused.

rows.why: Automation capex of about INR 9.5 crore is planned over 12-15 months funded from internal accruals, but utilisation was not disclosed, so a larger capacity capex call cannot be made from this brief.

rows.why: Q2 total income up 58.6%, EBITDA up 103.8% and H1 income up 47%, with management guiding more than 30% for FY27 and FY28 and revenue potentially reaching INR 500 crore 'next year or maybe year after' versus INR 300 crore in FY26.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Tin, copper and steel inflation (average near 50% YoY per management), the Europe INR 35-40 crore pipeline taking 9-12 months to convert, and Hormuz shipping disruption could pressure margins and delay the INR 131 crore FY28 additional business.

rows.why: US customers hold about 3 months of inventory and management says the build is complete, with future inventory rising only modestly with volume, though air freight costs rise where Hormuz disruption extends shipping.

rows.label: Automation and productivity gains
rows.why: Automation and robotic cells (about INR 9.5 crore total) with 2.5-3.5 year ROI and AI visual inspection in 9-12 months support the 25% productivity claim and the 23% margin target, though the brief gives no quantified savings.

524000|2026-03.headline: Poonawalla Fincorp Q4 FY26 PAT rose 69.6% QoQ to ₹255 crore, NIM recovered to 9.05% and ROA to 1.81%, with credit cost down to 2.51%.
524000|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 showed sequential gains across margin, credit cost, opex and profit: NIM rose 43 bps QoQ to 9.05%, credit cost fell to 2.51% from 2.62%, and Opex-to-AUM dropped to 4.13%. PAT reached ₹255 crore (up 69.6% QoQ) and full-year PAT was ₹542 crore. Asset quality improved across Stages 1, 2 and 3, with GNPA at 1.44% and 6MoB30+ at 1.05%. Management reiterated ROA as its North Star metric and said it expects ROA to keep improving, while investments in AI, branches and technology continue. A ₹2,500 crore QIP in April 2026 lifted the pro-forma CAR to 20.74%.

segments.name: Prime personal loans (PL Prime)
segments.commentary: Monthly disbursement run rate about ₹468 crore at end-March 2026; 33% of Q4 disbursements straight-through digital, up from 28% in Q3, with a target of 35-40%. Over 70% of customers have bureau scores of 750+.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: 400 gold branches operationalised as committed; Q4 disbursement about ₹819 crore; over 90% of branches in Tier 2 and Tier 3 locations.

segments.name: Consumer durables
segments.commentary: 12,500+ retail outlets across 240 locations; target to at least double consumer durable customer count in FY27; peak month of over 54,000 cases.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: Average monthly disbursals about ₹125 crore in Q4, up about 18% QoQ; FY26 disbursements ₹1,000 crore; used CVs are 70%+ of volume.

segments.name: Education loans
segments.commentary: Launched a year ago; over 22,000 files processed and about ₹900 crore disbursed cumulatively; around 500+ consultants and partners; instant sanction about 20% of sanctions.

segments.name: Six new businesses
segments.commentary: Contributed close to 24% of disbursements in Q4 vs 20% in Q3 FY26.

guidance_outlook: NIM expected to keep improving; management says disbursement yield gains will gradually feed into portfolio yield.
Credit cost seen as fairly robust from here on; 6MoB30+ expected to stay range-bound and trend lower as gold and PL Prime grow in mix.
FY27 AUM growth guidance of 35-40% with commensurate disbursements; management said it could be a notch better.
Opex-to-AUM targeted lower by end of FY27 than current levels, but expected to fluctuate 10-25 bps QoQ with branch clustering and investment trajectory.
ROA expected to move strength-to-strength over the next few quarters; no intermediate ROA guidance given.
Fee income expected to show strength in FY27 but no numerical guidance given.
Customer service AI bot expected to reach 80-85% autonomous resolution over the next two quarters; three agentic funnel agents due in Q2 FY27 to lift digital loan conversion by over 15%.
capex_capacity: 400 gold branches operationalised by March 2026; future branch openings planned along similar lines to last year, with front-end investment and clustering causing QoQ opex swings.
Consumer durables onboarding exceeded the ~12,000-outlet plan for the start of the year; aim to at least double consumer durable customer count over FY27.
AI: 42 of 76 identified AI projects deployed, 34 under development; token consumption above 30 million per month, up more than 100x YoY.
Credit AI for underwriters lets PL headcount process 1.2x the volume; no new PL underwriters hired during FY26 growth.
Collections: tech-enabled collection system being built with decoupled collection vectors; bucket flow improved 2x vs prior year.
demand_pricing: Disbursement yield at 15.96%, up 40 bps QoQ; management cited pricing power as a key driver of NIM recovery.
Management said disbursements may reach one-third of book this year, supporting NIM and ROA.
Business loans run at low-to-mid teens growth; pre-owned car loans also held to low teens; LAP growth strong, restricted to tickets above ₹50 lakh.
Management said it is not doing micro-LAPs and has no exposure to small-ticket LAP segments, and cited the Middle East conflict as a watch item but no current stress.
Stage 1 assets 97.5% (97.4% in Q3 FY26); Stage 2 1.1%; Stage 3 1.44%; provisioning coverage 49%.

qa_highlights.question: What are disbursement yield and book yield for the quarter, and is the geopolitical situation a risk to asset quality or provisioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited disbursement yield of 15.96% (up 40 bps QoQ) and said portfolio yield will catch up gradually. On the geopolitical question it said exposure is within risk tolerance, with stress testing done; LAP tickets are above ₹50 lakh, and gold and salaried-PL exposure are low-risk, so no risk was seen. Management is closely watching the environment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state level for 6MoB30+ at 1.05%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 6MoB30+ would be range-bound at current levels, with downward trend as gold loans and PL Prime grow in AUM share. GNPA was described as the lead indicator of credit cost.

qa_highlights.question: Guidance on fee income?
qa_highlights.answer: No numerical guidance was given. Management expects fee income strength in FY27 from processing fees, insurance and cross-sell, with growth now more calibrated after the launch phase.

qa_highlights.question: Status of technology and AI journey?
qa_highlights.answer: PL Prime is about 30% digital of a ₹480-500 crore monthly-scale business and expected to rise to 30-40%. Business loan digitisation is planned in 6-9 months. AI projects are cutting manpower needs, with no new PL underwriters hired.

qa_highlights.question: Path to ROA and FY27 disbursement and AUM plans?
qa_highlights.answer: ROA expected to keep improving over the next few quarters, with no interim guidance. FY27 AUM growth guided at 35-40% with commensurate disbursements. Opex-to-AUM expected lower by March 2027, with 10-25 bps QoQ swings.

qa_highlights.question: How will negative long-term ALM be bridged?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ₹2,500 crore capital raise bridges the gap; the reply came from a speaker not on the management list.

risks_watch: Geopolitical and external-environment risk on the ~50% unsecured book; management says it is monitoring but sees no current risk.
Opex-to-AUM may fluctuate 10-25 bps QoQ with branch openings, and fee income has no numerical guidance.
Credit cost sustainability: 6MoB30+ is 1.05% and GNPA 1.44%; lower credit cost depends on gold and PL Prime mix shift.
Execution of AI agent rollouts (customer service bot to 80-85% autonomous resolution; three agents due Q2 FY27) and cost-to-serve gains.
Long-term ALM gap management and funding cost (7.63%) after the QIP.

524164|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR619 crore (+17.4% YoY) and EBITDA margin rose 251 bps to 15.2%, helped by Ibuprofen demand recovery and higher prices.

EBITDA rose about 40% to INR94 crore, with margin up 251 bps to 15.2%, and PAT rose 68% to about INR53 crore. For FY26, revenue grew 11.5% to INR2,319 crore, EBITDA grew about 29% to INR290 crore (margin 12.4% vs 10.7%), and PAT rose about 36% to INR138 crore. Management attributed the gains to utilisation, product mix, non-Ibuprofen traction and a late-quarter price uptick that was partly offset by raw material cost increases.

524164|2026-06.headline: IOL Chemicals Q1 FY27 revenue rose 37% YoY to INR756 crore and PAT 90% to INR64.5 crore, with EBITDA margin at 14.6%.

524164|2026-09.headline: IOL Chemicals Q2 FY27 revenue rose ~40% YoY to INR795 crore and EBITDA margin expanded to 14.4%, with PAT of INR65 crore (up ~117%).

EBITDA rose about 80% YoY to INR115 crore, a 14.4% margin (up 321 bps), and PAT more than doubled in H1 to about INR130 crore. Management guided FY27 revenue growth to 25%+ (revised up from 15-20%) and EBITDA margin of 14-15%, and said prices of key products have been stable for 2-3 quarters. Three projects worth about INR500 crore were announced, to be funded from internal accruals.

qa_highlights.question: Will incremental ibuprofen capacity go to merchant or formulation customers?

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and borrowing needs for the rest of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What asset turn and margins are expected in CDMO and the overall business?

qa_highlights.question: What is the specialty chemicals toll-manufacturing arrangement?

524200|2026-03.headline: Vinati Organics FY26 standalone EBITDA rose 17% to INR741 crores and PAT 18% to INR488 crores, with the company still debt-free.
524200|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone net income including other income rose 17% QoQ to INR631 crores, EBITDA grew 20% QoQ to INR203 crores and PAT rose 27% QoQ to INR137 crores. For FY26, standalone net income was flat at INR2,281 crores while EBITDA and PAT grew 17% and 18%. Demand softened from October 2025 and management says it has since recovered. IBB volumes fell about 20% versus FY25 because of raw material unavailability linked to the Iran war, which management says is now resolved. Management guides about 15% company-level volume growth in FY27 and FY27 capex of INR200-250 crores.

segments.name: ATBS
segments.commentary: Roughly one-third of FY26 revenue; management expects about 15% volume growth YoY for at least the next three years. Plant running at about 80% utilisation (about 75% post-expansion). Phase 2 of the expansion comes into effect by October 2026, with fuller utilisation in FY28.

segments.name: Antioxidants (AO)
segments.commentary: Roughly 15-20% of FY26 revenue; revenue grew 15% in FY26. Management said FY26 AO volume was roughly flat-to-5% up, and the anti-dumping duty (ADD) application was rejected and reapplied, with a decision 6-9 months away.

segments.name: IB and HP-MTBE
segments.commentary: Roughly 10-12% of FY26 revenue; stable in FY26, with management expecting double-digit growth in FY27.

segments.name: IBB
segments.commentary: Roughly 10-12% of FY26 revenue; volume fell about 20% versus FY25 due to raw material unavailability linked to the Iran war, now reported as resolved.

segments.name: Butyl phenols
segments.commentary: Capacity about 50,000 tonnes running at roughly 70-75% utilisation; management expects moderate growth in FY27 with no room for further expansion, so incremental demand goes first to captive use.

segments.name: Customised and others
segments.commentary: Grew 10% YoY in FY26 on higher customer demand. Remainder of revenue mix.

segments.name: VOPL (100% subsidiary)
segments.commentary: FY26 sales were only about INR10 crores. Process reengineering of about 6 months to finish by September 2026, with production from October and revenue of about INR100-120 crores expected in FY27, from Q2/Q3.

CWIP was about INR210 crores at year-end, of which about INR60-70 crores is yet to be capitalised at VOPL. About INR120-125 crores of VOPL CWIP is expected to be capitalised in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY26 revenue mix by product?

qa_highlights.question: What is the VOPL revenue outlook?

qa_highlights.question: How much capex is planned in VOPL and how much CWIP is there?

qa_highlights.question: What is the ATBS capacity and cost of the two expansion phases?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is about 50,000 tonnes (about 40,000 tonnes for higher-purity grades) with 10,000 tonnes per phase. The two phases cost about INR250-300 crores in total.

qa_highlights.question: Will AO and butyl phenol revenue reach the targeted INR700-800 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plan is on track, with AO and butyl phenol revenue in the INR800-900 crore range within the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a 26-27% EBITDA margin is a reasonable long-term level given expansions, new products and raw material swings.

rows.why: Utilisation is about 80% in ATBS and butyl phenols are at 70-75% with no room to expand, and management has already guided INR200-250 crores for FY27 and INR250-300 crores a year for 3-5 years, so further capex plans are likely to be firmed up.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA rose 20% QoQ and PAT 27% QoQ, and the Iran-war raw material disruption is resolved, but the FY27 guide of about 15% volume growth rests on recovery that is not yet proven.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: AO faces Chinese undercutting with FY26 growth of about 5%, the anti-dumping decision is 6-9 months away, and VOPL revenue of INR100-120 crores in FY27 depends on a reengineering that had teething troubles.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: H2 FY27, with revenue mainly from FY28
rows.why: Management expects two to three new downstream products in H2 FY27 from the MEHQ, butyl phenol, antioxidant and VOPL pipeline (TAA, PTAP, 4-MAP).

rows.label: VOPL revenue ramp to INR100-120 crores in FY27
rows.why: VOPL sales were about INR10 crores in FY26; process reengineering of about 6 months must finish by September 2026 and the plant had teething troubles, so the ramp depends on that timeline.

rows.label: AO anti-dumping duty decision
rows.why: ADD was rejected and reapplied, with 80-90% of sector applications rejected historically, and AO revenue grew only about 15% in FY26 with volume roughly flat to 5% up under Chinese undercutting.

rows.label: IBB volume recovery after Iran-war disruption
rows.why: IBB volume fell about 20% versus FY25 on raw material unavailability, which management now says is resolved, but no recovery figures were given.

tone.note: Management was confident on the debt-free model, ATBS demand, formula-based pricing and margins, and openly acknowledged the October 2025 slowdown; it was cautious and somewhat evasive on AO growth, the anti-dumping duty outcome and the VOPL timeline after teething troubles.

524208|2026-03.headline: Aarti Industries Q4 FY26 revenue rose 9% YoY to INR 2,422 crore and EBITDA 29% to INR 342 crore, with FY27 capex guided at INR 700-800 crore.
524208|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 2,422 crore (up 9% YoY), EBITDA INR 342 crore (up 29%) and PAT INR 137 crore (up 43%), helped by volume growth and higher utilisation. West Asia disruption raised benzene, sulfur, aniline, toluene and methanol prices by over 60%, lifted freight costs and cut Middle East shipments, which are about 9-10% of revenue. Zone IV projects are delayed 3-4 months on contract labour shortages, with the bulk now expected in FY27. Management guided FY27 capex to INR 700-800 crore and aims to reduce net debt in FY27 despite working-capital pressure.

segments.name: Energy applications
segments.commentary: About 40% of revenue; volumes down 4% QoQ on lower Middle East exports. Expansion to 360 KTPA is on track and expected to commission soon. Middle East is about 9-10% of company revenue, mostly energy.

segments.name: Agrochemicals
segments.commentary: Steady volume growth but margin pressure continues. A new $150 million multiyear agro intermediate contract runs to March 2030 with no incremental capex.

segments.name: Polymers
segments.commentary: Strong growth phase on EV-linked demand; MPDA continues to underperform due to Chinese competition.

segments.name: Dyes, pigments and paints
segments.commentary: Share of revenue about 10-11%. Demand pressure in 3,3'-DCBH globally, partly offset by domestic demand; some low-margin demand destruction possible in 3-6 months.

segments.name: Pharma
segments.commentary: Stable in the quarter; PNCB chain expected to benefit from China anti-involution from Q1 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex guided at INR 700-800 crore (about INR 150 crore a year is maintenance), funding Zone IV completion and a new INR 200-250 crore backward-integration contract.
Zone IV: calcium chloride and multipurpose plant to be commercialised within the quarter; remaining blocks commissioned through FY27 after a 3-4 month delay; initial revenue from Q2 FY27.
Management aims to reduce net debt in FY27 despite higher working capital, as capex intensity falls and cash flow improves.
Tax rate guided at about 9-15% going forward.
Working capital target of 55-60 days, with the company currently above this level.
Augene (Superform JV) to commission around June-July 2026; recycling JV to commission in CY26.
Interest-cost and EBITDA potential from Zone IV and the UPL JV unchanged at INR 300-450 crore, but realisation may slip 6-7 months.
capex_capacity: Zone IV total capex about INR 1,800-2,000 crore; gross block expected at INR 9,500-10,000 crore by end FY27.
Energy expansion to 360 KTPA on track for commissioning soon.
Contract labour availability in the capex region down 35%, delaying last-mile pipeline work.
Augene JV and recycling JV commissioning in 2026; DCB debottlenecking under way.
About 50% of the Bayer/Dicamba-linked asset is used for one intermediate, with steady volumes.
demand_pricing: Raw material prices (benzene, sulfur, aniline, toluene, methanol) rose over 60% in the quarter; some more than doubled.
Agro pricing is up sharply from January, but the company is holding spreads rather than absolute prices; full pass-through expected over 3-6 months.
NCB margins and pricing improved on China's anti-involution policy; DCB remains robust on EV demand.
MMA economics are volatile with gasoline-naphtha cracks ranging from negative to up $20/bbl; Middle East shipments physically halted, US shipments steady, Europe starting.
Physical supply of methanol (about a couple of months' cover) and sulfur (a few weeks' cover) is secure.

qa_highlights.question: Was there an inventory gain in Q4 margins, especially in March?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory impact was not significant; FX gain was about INR 10 crore in the quarter, and raw material costs also rose in March.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: About 9-10% of revenue on an annual average basis, mostly energy; product is being redirected elsewhere, with the full impact visible in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did FY27 capex fall and what is the breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 capex was INR 1,125 crore as guided, not reduced; FY27 guided at INR 700-800 crore mainly for Zone IV, the new long-term contract and about INR 150 crore maintenance.

qa_highlights.question: Why is debt high despite about INR 600 crore cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash was a late-March term loan disbursement; net debt is about INR 4,300 crore, with bulk of cash used to repay debt in early April. Working capital rose INR 250-300 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 freight and other-expense jump and inventory build?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight rates rose from mid-February, exports were 57% of revenue, and US mix lengthened voyages; INR 409 crore stock build reflects goods in transit not yet recognised as revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Are Zone IV EBITDA and the net debt/EBITDA target at risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost and operating-leverage initiatives are on track; the EBITDA potential is unchanged but may slip 6-7 months. Net debt/EBITDA was about 3.6x at year-end.

risks_watch: Middle East flows halted for 6-8 weeks; full Q1 FY27 impact on energy volumes depends on West Asia stabilisation.
Working capital and net debt rise if crude moves to USD 140-150/bbl.
Zone IV labour shortage and 3-4 month delay; check commissioning and first revenue in Q2 FY27.
Potential demand destruction in low-margin dyes and pigments over 3-6 months.
Unhedged USD 87 million FX loan; further rupee depreciation would add revaluation losses.
MPDA and agro margins remain under pressure from Chinese competition.

key_quotes: The overall demand environment for our basket of products remained largely stable.
Our capex for FY27 is expected to be in the range of INR 700 crore to INR800 crore as we continue our journey to optimize capex and maximize the returns.

rows.why: Zone IV total capex about INR 1,800-2,000 crore with gross block rising to INR 9,500-10,000 crore by end FY27, energy expansion to 360 KTPA near commissioning, and Augene JV due June-July 2026, though labour shortage (down 35%) delays the last-mile work 3-4 months.
